# Audio (walkie-talkie)

The robot carries a speaker and a microphone. The `Audio` tool on the control home turns the app into a walkie-talkie: listen to what the robot hears, and hold a button to talk through its speaker.

## Opening the popover

Tap `Audio` (the microphone icon) in the right card (`OBSERVE`). The popover is titled `Walkie-talkie` `· Robot speaker/mic`. A green dot on the `Audio` button means listening is currently on.

![Walkie-talkie popover](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-audio.pc.en.png)

## Listening

`Listen to robot audio` is a toggle. Switch it on and the robot's microphone streams to your device until you switch it off. The label under it reads `Listening` or `Off`. Listening stays on when you close the popover — the dot on the `Audio` button reminds you.

## Volume

Three sliders, each showing its value in percent (defaults 80 / 70 / 65 %):

| Slider | Controls |
|---|---|
| `Robot speaker` | Loudness of your voice out of the robot. |
| `Robot mic` | Gain of the robot's microphone (what you hear when listening). |
| `My volume` | Playback level on your own device. |

The app stores the last values you set and restores them on the next start.

## Push to talk

Talking is not in the popover. Press and **hold** the `Walkie-talkie` button at the bottom right of the control home — next to the right joystick, or at the right edge when a gamepad is connected. While you hold it the button turns green and reads `Talking`. Release it to stop. The app sends your voice only while you hold the button, so nothing goes out by accident — the popover's footer reminds you: `To talk, hold [Walkie-talkie] at the bottom right`.

The first time you press the button the app asks for microphone permission. If you refuse (or no microphone can be opened), the `Walkie-talkie` button turns amber and the popover's footer changes to `No mic permission — allow it in app settings`. Grant it in the operating system's app settings and try again.

## Robot speaker power

If the robot's speaker amplifier is switched off you will see `Robot speaker power is off` in the popover, and the `Walkie-talkie` button is dimmed and cannot be pressed. Tap `Turn on` in that banner to power the amplifier and talk again.

## Platform notes

- **Audio channel** — `Robot audio channel failed — check the robot connection` in the footer means the audio link to the robot could not be set up. Check that the robot is connected (video is streaming) and press `Walkie-talkie` again.
- **Choosing your own speaker/microphone** — only when the app runs in a web browser: a `My devices` block lists `Speaker (output)` and `Microphone (applies from next PTT)`. Each list appears only when the browser reports devices of that kind, and the speaker list also needs a browser that supports output switching — Chrome does, some others do not. If no device has a name yet (Device 1, Device 2…), tap `Show device names — allow mic permission`. The Android, iOS, and desktop apps use whatever audio devices the system is on, so this block is hidden.
- **`My mic` `Send gain`** — shown only in browsers that still support a microphone volume constraint. Current Chrome does not, so most people never see it.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/camera-vision.html
================================================================================

# Camera & Vision

The center of the control home is the viewport. It shows either the live 3D pose of the robot or one of its camera streams, and it is where tap-to-go and the vision overlays live.

![Control home with the viewport](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home.pc.en.png)

## Switching the viewport source

Tap the source name at the top center of the viewport to open the source list. The list shows only the sources whose cameras the robot actually reports, so it is shorter on robots with fewer cameras.

| Source | Shows | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `3D` | Live 3D pose of the robot (always available) | — |
| `Front` / `Rear` / `Left` / `Right` | A single body camera | That camera |
| `Stairs` | Stair-climbing view composed from the front, rear, and belly cameras | Front, rear, and all four belly cameras |
| `Quad` | Four body cameras in one 2×2 frame | Front, rear, left, and right cameras |
| `Panorama` | Four body cameras stitched horizontally | Front, rear, left, and right cameras |
| `CCTV` | The optional PTZ unit's color camera | PTZ color camera (see [PTZ camera](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/ptz.html)) |
| `Thermal` | The PTZ unit's thermal camera | PTZ thermal sensor |
| `PTZ Mix` | Color and thermal combined | PTZ color camera and thermal sensor |
| `SLAM` | Live SLAM map | LiDAR |

The video keeps its 16:9 shape and fits into the space below the top bar. On wide screens, the leftover side gutters hold the cards and virtual joysticks. The source list never covers the top bar, so the E-STOP stays reachable while the menu is open.

## View options (right card)

The right card, titled `OBSERVE`, holds what you look at and listen to. Tap its round button to fold the card into a circle or open it again. The card starts open, and the app remembers your choice.

- `Vision` — opens the `Vision` popover: the `Point to Go` switch (see below) and vision toggles such as `Night mode` and `Dock scan`.

| Row | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Night mode` | Low-light capture |
| `Stealth` | LEDs and indicators off |
| `GUIDE` | Drive guide lines drawn into the video |
| `FACE` | Face detection boxes |
| `Dock scan` | Look for docking markers |
| `Heightmap` | Terrain elevation overlay. `└ Edge emphasis` below it is enabled only while `Heightmap` is on |

- `3D scene` — opens `3D scene settings`. Shown only while the `3D` source is selected.
- `Audio` — opens the walkie-talkie (see [Audio](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/audio.html)).

`Speed HUD`, `Gyro widget`, and `Video resolution` are in **App settings › App settings**.

`3D scene settings` holds:

- `Grid` — Grid ON / Grid OFF plus a grid size in meters (`−` / `+` or type a value).
- `Scene theme` — background color presets.
- `Camera behavior` — `Top`, `Robot`, or `3D` camera follow mode.
- `LiDAR (display)` — `Off` / `On` for the point cloud.

## Tap-to-go (P2G)

With `Point to Go` on, tapping a point on the ground in the front camera makes the robot walk to it. An aim marker appears where you press and **follows your finger as you drag**, and the command goes to wherever you lift your finger, so you can line the point up before you let go. **Drag off the video before you release and nothing is sent** — that is how you cancel a press you did not mean. The robot itself draws the path and target on the video it streams, so the marker is only momentary feedback.

A tap moves the robot only when **all four** of these are true:

1. `Point to Go` is switched on in the `Vision` popover (the viewport shows a blue border while it is on).
2. The viewport source is `Front`. On every other source the switch is grayed out and reads `Front camera source only`, because the app reads the tap in front-camera coordinates.
3. The robot is standing and ready to walk. The app does not check this — the robot decides whether to act on the command.
4. You tapped **ground that is visible in the image**. The app sends every tap, but the robot walks only when the point lands on ground it can see. A tap on the horizon, a wall, or the sky shows the marker and does nothing else.

::: warning
While `Point to Go` is on, the whole video area is a tap target — an accidental touch sends a walk command. Turn it off as soon as you are done.
:::

## Docking-marker overlay

![Docking-marker overlay on the front camera](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-dock-scan.pc.en.png)

When the robot sees a docking marker (ArUco), a `Start docking` button appears over the video — on `3D` and on every camera source, including **Front**, **Rear** and **Stairs**. On the sources that show the camera which found it, the app draws a box around the marker itself. The other sources show a picture of the docking marker at the bottom of the screen instead — tapping it also starts docking.

`Dock scan` in the `Vision` popover switches the robot's marker detection on and off; the detection itself runs on the camera images. It is on by default. While docking runs, the marker is drawn no matter what this toggle says — watching it is the whole point.

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#vision).

## Dock View

![Dock View during a docking run](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-dock-view.pc.en.png)

Starting docking opens **Dock View**. It replaces the viewport with the three cameras the robot uses for docking and shows what the robot detects, so you can tell why a docking run succeeds or fails.

Closing it does not stop docking. While the run is under way, the docking banner stays at the top of the screen, and `Tap to view` on the banner opens Dock View again.

::: warning
**Dock View exists only during a docking run.** The banner disappears four seconds after docking completes, and it is not shown at all once a run has failed — from then on there is no way back into the screen. Watch a run while it is happening — to see the cameras again, you have to start another docking run.
:::

The video band holds three panes: **FRONT**, **REAR**, and **BOTTOM2** (the downward infrared camera). The pane whose camera found the marker is outlined in orange, and a box and the marker axes are drawn on the marker. The pane label also shows the marker IDs used and, for **BOTTOM2**, whether the IR projector is on.

Below the band:

- **Progress** — `Approach 1`, `Approach 2`, `Approach 3`, `Sit`, `Charge`. `Charge` lights up only once the robot measures charging current.
- **Status** — the current step in words, and the reason when a run fails.
- **Detection hints** — shown when the robot keeps discarding the marker, for example `Marker detection quality is low`. When a run has ended because no marker was found, the hint also says what to do.
- **Buttons** — `Stop docking` while docking runs; `Undock` once the robot is charging; `Resume docking` after a failed run; `Stand up` when all retries are used; `Close` at any time.

`Undock` and `Stand up` lift a seated robot, so they are press-and-hold buttons. Hold one and it fills from the left. The command goes out the moment the fill reaches the far edge, about a second later. Let go before it is full and nothing is sent.

While the robot retries on its own, the buttons read `Retrying automatically` and there is nothing for you to do.

Once docking finishes, the charge level appears after three seconds. Five seconds later the cameras turn themselves off and the band reads `Docking finished — the camera view is turned off`. A docked robot sits on the charger for hours, so there is nothing left to watch.

![Dock View after the cameras are turned off](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-dock-view-off.pc.en.png)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html
================================================================================

# Connection

The **hub** decides *which robot the app talks to*. It is the first screen you see after startup. The robot name and connection state sit at the top left, and the `Control` button at the bottom right opens the control home once the robot is connected — before that it reads `Opens once connected`. Nothing on these screens is sent to the robot itself.

On the very first start — no saved robot and no account — the app opens the **Access code** screen instead. Press `Skip` to go straight to the hub, and the app starts looking for a robot on the robot's network on its own.

## Status line

![The hub status line](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/hub.pc.en.png)

The robot name has a colored dot in front and the state after it:

| Text | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Connect to the robot's WiFi` | No robot is saved yet |
| `Not connected` | A robot is selected but not connected |
| `Connecting…` | A connection attempt is in progress |
| `Connected` · route | The app is talking to the robot — the route is `local network`, `Public IP`, or `remote`, and the battery follows |
| `Connection failed` · reason | The attempt failed — press `Reconnect` |
| `Not on the robot's WiFi` | The robot is on its own network, but this device is on another one |
| `Remote — access code needed` | A remote robot is selected but the access code is not stored — press `Enter code` |

When the device is on the wrong network the line names the robot's WiFi if the app knows it (*Robot WiFi(SSID) — please switch to it*). On Linux desktop and Steam Deck, the `Switch WiFi` button next to it joins that network directly, or opens the network list. On Android, `WiFi settings` opens the system Wi-Fi screen.

## Selecting a robot

![Select robot](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/hub-robots.pc.en.png)

Tap the robot name (▾) to open **Select robot**. It lists the robots saved on this device, plus the robots assigned to your account while you are logged in. A robot that is both appears once, matched by serial number. Each row shows the serial, the route (`local network` with the WiFi name, `Public IP`, or `remote`), and when you last used it. Tap a row to connect.

The dot on each row shows the robot's state: green = connected, blue = on (its WiFi is in range), gray = off or unknown.

- **Linux desktop / Steam Deck**: the list scans nearby WiFi every time it opens, and `Refresh` scans again; while the scan runs the dots stay gray rather than showing the previous result (a scan can take up to 15 seconds). Tapping a robot whose WiFi is not in range does not connect — the row reads *No signal from the robot's WiFi*. If the robot's WiFi is saved on the device and in range, the app switches to it before connecting, and the status line names the network it is switching to. If it cannot switch, a dialog says why (*Can't find the robot's WiFi*, *WiFi password needed*, *Couldn't switch to the robot's WiFi*) and the previous robot stays selected. A network whose password was never entered cannot be joined this way — join it once with `Select WiFi`.
- **Android / iOS**: the app cannot read or change Wi-Fi, so the dot is only green or gray. Switch in the system settings; the status line tells you which network to pick.
- A robot that is also assigned to your account connects directly if it answers on its local network, and remotely if it does not.

The slider icon on a row opens that robot's profile, where you can change its `Name` or delete it with the trash icon. Deleting removes the robot from this device only — server assignments are handled in the dashboard. Remote-only robots have no profile to edit.

At the bottom, `Simulator` (`In-app physics sim`) opens the control home with the in-app simulator instead of a robot, and `Add robot` opens the screen below.

## Adding a robot

![Add robot](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/hub-add-robot.pc.en.png)

**Add robot** offers the ways to reach a robot. Once a robot answers, it is saved by its serial number and the app returns to the hub.

### Robot WiFi

Join the robot's WiFi (AP) and the app finds it — on its own network the robot always sits at `192.168.0.10`. The check runs when the screen opens (unless a robot is already connected) and again with `Check again`. A new robot is named after the WiFi it was found on; rename it from its profile.

- `Select WiFi` (Linux desktop / Steam Deck) opens the in-app network list. The app checks for the robot again when you close it. A saved network shows a spinner and `Connecting…` on its row while it joins.
- `WiFi settings` (Android) opens the system Wi-Fi screen.
- If nothing answers: *No robot answered — check the robot's power and that this device is on the robot's AP.*
- If the robot found is the one already connected, the app says so instead of adding it again — switch to the other robot's WiFi and check again.

In the browser (web) build, this card just says *The app (APK/desktop) searches automatically.*

### Connect by address

The browser (web) build, the desktop app and Steam Deck also offer **Connect by address**, for a robot behind a router, the simulator on this PC, or a robot with a public IP.

- `local network` — enter the `Robot IP` (preset to `192.168.0.10`). `Connect` first checks that a robot answers at that address. If none does, nothing is saved (*No robot responded at this address — check the IP and robot power*). `This PC · 127.0.0.1` fills in the local simulator address.
- `Public IP` — enter the `Public IP or domain`. If the robot has a WebRTC token set, enter the same value in `WebRTC token (only if set on the robot)`. Ports 8080 and 8081 must be reachable from your network.

The address takes effect only if you opened the page at `localhost` on the PC that runs the proxy. From another device the app shows *The proxy could not switch the target — check that you opened this page via localhost on this PC.* — restart the proxy with `--robot <new IP>` instead.

### Access code

`Enter access code` opens the keypad. Enter the 4-digit code from the dashboard one time, and the robots assigned to your account show up in **Select robot** and connect remotely over LTE from then on. The robot does not need a public IP.

The **Profile** button at the top right shows the account and the number of `assigned robots`. `Log out` drops the account's remote robots from the list. Robots saved on this device stay.

::: warning
The access code is a credential. Do not share it, and use `Log out` on a shared device.
:::

## Automatic connection

The app connects on its own in these cases:

- **Start-up** — the app checks the robot's network first. If a robot answers, it is added (or updated) and connected, and the app skips the hub and opens the control home. If none answers, the desktop app — not Steam Deck — connects to a MuJoCo simulator running on the same PC, and if there is no simulator either, it selects the robot you used most recently.
- **Network change** — when the device joins a robot's WiFi, the app checks the robot's serial number and connects to it, adding it to the list if it is new. This also moves a remote connection to the direct one when you come within range.

A robot without a serial number is still saved and listed. The app tells those robots apart by their WiFi name.

## My device WiFi

The WiFi chip in the control home's top bar shows the signal strength. Tap it to see **My device WiFi** — the network your device is on and whether it is the robot's network.

- The badge reads `Robot network` in green when your device address is in the same subnet as the robot IP. Otherwise it reads `Not robot network` in amber, with a warning that you cannot reach the robot until you join the robot AP. Both are hidden while you are connected remotely, since a remote connection does not use the robot's network.
- **Linux desktop / Steam Deck**: `Select WiFi` opens an in-app list of networks to join. `System settings` opens the OS network settings instead.
- **Android**: Android does not allow in-app scanning, so `System WiFi settings` opens the device's Wi-Fi settings screen. Pick the robot AP from the list, then press back to return to the app. The app needs location permission to show the SSID — tap the hint line to grant it. If you have already granted it and the name still does not appear, device location is off; tap the hint line to turn it on.
- iOS and web builds show a note to connect from the system settings instead.

## Connection status in the top bar {#connection-status-in-the-top-bar}

In the control home's top bar, the status light next to the logo summarizes the connection:

| Light | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Green | Everything is normal |
| Amber | Connected, but something needs attention — vision stream down, or another device holds control |
| Red, blinking fast | The robot reports a fault |
| Red | No connection to the robot |

Tap the light to open **Overall system status**. It lists **IMU**, **CAN**, **FindPose**, **Control**, **Vision**, and **Ownership**, each with a green or amber dot. Tap a row marked `Run ▸` to retry that step. **Ownership** · `Take ▸` takes control back when another device is holding it.

The control home has no disconnected banner: if the robot drops and does not come back within 8 seconds, the app returns to the Hub, which is where the status line, `Reconnect`, and `Switch WiFi` live. It also returns to the Hub the moment the connected robot changes — turning a robot off frees its WiFi, and the app may find a different robot on the robot network and connect to that one.

![Overall system status](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-status.pc.en.png)

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#connection).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/control-home.html
================================================================================

# Control home

The control home is the screen you drive the robot from. Open it with **Control** on the Hub. The whole screen is the viewport — a camera feed or the 3D view — with a motion card on the left, an **OBSERVE** card on the right, and two virtual joysticks in the lower corners when no gamepad is connected.

![Control home](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home.pc.en.png)

::: danger
Every motion button on this screen moves the real robot. **Keep people, animals, and obstacles at least 2 m clear of the robot whenever it is operating.** Check your surroundings before you press anything, and keep a hand near `E-STOP`.
:::

## Top bar

The top bar floats over the video in two groups. From left to right:

| Element | What it shows / does |
|---|---|
| Logo | Goes to the **Hub**. The robot stops where it is and stays connected |
| Status light | A green, amber, or red light that pulses slowly — fast when something is critical, and a steady red while not connected. Tap it for **Overall system status** (see [Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html#connection-status-in-the-top-bar)) |
| Gait chip | The robot's current gait name, such as `STANDING`, colored by state. Hidden while not connected |
| `SLAM` chip | Appears only while external control (SLAM or SDK) is active. Tap it to hand control back to the app |
| Signal bars | WiFi signal strength, and how fast data is moving over the robot link |
| Log badge | Unread log alerts |
| **Robot** battery, device battery | The robot pack's charge, with a charging mark while it charges, and your own device's battery |
| `E-STOP` | Emergency stop — see below |
| Quit | Desktop build only. Asks **Quit the app?** first, then closes the app. The robot keeps running |

If the robot drops off and does not come back within 8 seconds, the app takes you to the Hub on its own, because that is where you reconnect. It also goes back to the Hub the moment the connected robot changes, so you never end up driving a robot you did not pick.

### E-STOP

`E-STOP` never fires on a single tap. Pressing it opens the confirmation **Emergency stop?**, which warns that *The robot immediately stops all motion and cuts power. Reinitialization is required to resume control.* Press **Stop** to go ahead or **Cancel** to back out. The button behaves the same way on every screen, even with a menu open.

![E-STOP confirmation](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-estop.pc.en.png)

::: warning
After an emergency stop the robot has no motor power. Bring it back with **Auto Start** (below) before it can move again. The step chips show you where the sequence stopped.
:::

### Ownership

Only one device controls the robot at a time. When another device holds control, the status light turns amber and the **Ownership** row in **Overall system status** reads `Take ▸` — tap it to take control back. While a SLAM or SDK program is driving, you get the `SLAM` chip instead.

## Auto Start

Until the robot's motor control is running, a green **Auto Start** pill sits at the bottom center of the viewport, grayed out while not connected. Tap it to open the **Auto Start** dialog. The dialog always stays centered on the screen: when the screen is short, only the **Startup sequence** list inside it scrolls and the buttons stay visible. On a short screen such as a phone in landscape, each step shows as one line — tap it to open or close its details. The running step and any failed or warning step open by themselves.

1. Read the instruction — *Place the robot on a flat floor, and make sure all feet and knees contact the ground.*
2. Five step chips lay out the sequence: **POWER**, **CAN-BUS**, **HOMING**, **IMU-CHECK**, **START**. Tap an unfinished **CAN-BUS** or **HOMING** chip to run just that step.
3. Press **Auto Start**. The dialog stays open and the **Startup sequence** panel below the chips fills in step by step — Pre-check, Leg Power, Joint comms, Motor parameters, Home position, IMU, Control active — marking each one **Passed / Failed / Warning / Running**.
4. If a step fails, the panel names the cause and the fix. For example: *The robot is already standing — Sit the robot down, then start again.* Take care of it and press **Start again**.
5. Press **Close** once the sequence reports **Done**. When a run you watched here clears the last step, **Start again** disappears and only **Close** remains, so you cannot start the sequence twice by accident.

You can also start the same sequence from the status light: **Overall system status › ▶ Auto start (full sequence)**.

## Viewport and source selector

The dropdown at the top center of the viewport picks what you see. `3D`, a live model of the robot, is always there. Camera sources show up only when the robot reports having that camera: **Front**, **Rear**, **Left**, **Right**, **Stairs**, **Quad**, **Panorama**, `CCTV`, **Thermal**, **PTZ Mix**, and `SLAM` on LiDAR robots. Tap outside the list to close it without changing the source.

Pick a PTZ-type source and the pan/tilt/zoom panel appears over the video. Drag it by its handle to move it.

While docking runs, the selector reads `Dock` and will not open — the viewport belongs to [Dock View](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/camera-vision.html#dock-view) until you close it.

## Left card — Motions

Everything that makes the robot move lives on the left.

- **Card**: folded, it is a round glass button with a walking-person icon. Tap it and the circle grows into the card; tap the card's top row to fold it back. The app remembers whether each card is open, and both start open.
- **Body**: the fixed motion buttons `SIT`, `STAND`, `WALK`, `STAIRS`, and `DOCKING` (only while docking is available), plus **Motions**, the dashed button that opens the full motion grid. Whichever button matches the robot's current gait is highlighted. See [Motion commands](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html).
- **Tool buttons**: a row of small buttons outside the card, just right of the left joystick — at the left edge in gamepad mode. Each one opens its panel above the row:
  - **Drive** — speed, body height, and tilt sliders ([Drive parameters](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html#drive-parameters)).
  - **Arm** — only on robots with a manipulator.
  - **CONTROL INPUT** — the input mode **Auto / Virtual / Pad** and the live gamepad map. *Auto* switches to a physical gamepad whenever one is connected. A green dot means external control is doing the driving.
- When the card is taller than the screen, a `▾` at the bottom tells you it scrolls.

## Right card — OBSERVE

Everything about *what you see and hear* lives on the right.

- **Card**: folded, it is a round glass button, and it opens and folds like the left card.
- **Body**:
  - **Vision** — the vision toggles, including **P2G** (Point-to-Go), which is available only while **Front** is the source. With P2G on, tapping a spot on the floor in the video sends the robot walking there.
  - **3D scene** — 3D view settings, shown only while `3D` is the source.
  - **Audio** — listen to the robot, volume, and devices. A green dot means listening is on.
  - `SLAM` — LiDAR robots only.
  - **PTZ** — robots with a PTZ camera only. Switches the view to the PTZ camera; tap again to go back to the source you were on.
- **Walkie-talkie**: the button at the bottom right, just left of the right joystick, or at the right edge in gamepad mode. Hold it to talk through the robot's speaker. It reads **Talking** for as long as you hold it, and it is grayed out while the speaker amplifier is off.
- **Gyro** and **Speed HUD** sit side by side at the bottom center of the video. Tap the gyro to enlarge it. You can turn both off in **App settings**.

::: warning
With **P2G** on, the whole video area is a command surface — every tap on the floor moves the robot. Turn it off when you are done.
:::

## Joysticks and input modes

- **Without a gamepad**, on touch devices and PCs, the screen shows two virtual joysticks. What the axes do depends on the current motion — see the axis tables in [Motion commands](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html).
- **With a gamepad**, whether a physical pad or a Steam Deck, the virtual joysticks disappear and you drive with the pad's sticks. Fold the cards to see more of the video.
- **One-stick mode** in App settings › Gamepad swaps the left and right stick roles so you can drive one-handed.

**Driving from the keyboard** — on a PC with no gamepad, the keyboard works alongside the virtual
joysticks. It works only on this screen: the same keys do nothing on the Hub or in settings.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> | Left stick — forward/back and sideways |
| <kbd>Q</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> | Right stick left / right — turn left / right |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Right stick |

The robot moves while you hold a key and stops when you let go. The keyboard has no emergency-stop
key — **E-STOP is the button at the top right of the screen**.

While connected, the bottom-left corner shows the current gait name as a small HUD.

## Compact layout

On short screens — phones, or a window less than 500 px tall — the layout stays the same and only the pieces get smaller. The joysticks, tool buttons, and walkie-talkie tuck into the corners, and the left card takes only the space above them and scrolls. On narrow screens the cards get narrower too. Nothing is taken away.

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#control-home).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/dashboard.html
================================================================================

# Dashboard

Open **Dashboard** with the `Dashboard` tile on the hub, which becomes active once the robot is connected. It lays the robot's live status out as cards, and in developer mode extra tabs add the robot state tables.

![Dashboard summary](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/dashboard.pc.en.png)

## Summary cards

### System

- **Robot S/N** — the serial number of the robot you are looking at, at the very top of the card. It reads `—` while not connected, or when the robot runs older software.
- **BATTERY** — charge in % with the pack voltage and a status word:
  - **Normal**
  - **Low** — below 15 %
  - **Low voltage — charge now** — below 10 % *and* pack voltage under 47 V. The numbers turn red. Stop work and charge.
  - **No signal** — no battery data received (for example in simulation).
- **ROBOT HEALTH** — **IMU**, **CAN**, **FindPose**, **Control**: each **Normal** or **Check**. The card badge reads **OK** when all are fine and **Check** otherwise.
- **ROBOT PC** — **CPU** load bar, **Temp**, **MEM** bar, and **Throttle** (**Normal** / **Throttled**).
- **DISTANCE (TRIP)** — **Total**, **Trip A**, **Trip B** in m, with **Reset A** / **Reset B** buttons.

### Joint·Pose

- **POSTURE** — an artificial-horizon dial with **Roll / Pitch / Yaw** (only when the gyro widget is enabled in settings), **GAIT_ID**, **Fall** (**Normal** or **FALL**), **RPY (°)**, **Height** in m, and **Battery A** (pack current).
- The badge shows the control-link state: **LIVE**, **Connecting**, or **Disconnected**.

### Config

- **PAYLOAD** — **Mounted slots**, **Total mass**, and **CoM X / Y / Z**, followed by the
  attached gear, each **Normal** or **Not detected**: **Robot arm** and **PTZ**. RAPID-variant
  robots also list **RCWS**, **RCGS**, and **CCTV**.
- **SENSOR** — **IMU**, **Front camera**, **Rear camera**, **Bottom camera 0** – **3**,
  **IR**, **Depth**, and **IR projector**, each **Normal** or **Not detected**.

A **Radiation (KHNP)** card appears only on KHNP-variant robots.

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#dashboard).

## Related

- Warnings and errors that affect these values are collected in [Logs](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html
================================================================================

# Developer mode

The app runs at the **operator tier** by default. Turning on developer mode adds diagnostic,
configuration and maintenance features to the screens. **Everything that only developer mode opens
is collected on this page** — the other pages cover what everyday operation needs.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Developer mode exposes <strong>commands that move the robot without the usual safeguards</strong> (joint lock, forced postures) and power controls that can cut the connection, the stance or driving. Turn it on only when you need it, and read each warning before you act.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Turning it on and off {#turn-on}

1. Tap the profile button at the top right of the hub.
2. Turn on the **Developer mode** toggle. The subtitle reads *Password required to turn on*.
3. Type the password in the **Developer mode password** dialog and press **Check**. A wrong password
   shows *Incorrect password* and clears the field.

Turning the toggle off returns to the operator tier immediately.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>The password is <strong>issued individually by Rainbow Robotics</strong>. It is not printed in this manual — do not share the one you were given. To request it, use <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/">Support</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>

### When an account sets the tier {#by-account}

Logging in with an access code (`Log in with access code` in the profile menu) sets the tier **from
your account**. While logged in the profile menu shows the account and its level instead of the
Developer mode toggle. Press `Log out` in the same menu to return to the normal tier.

## What each screen gains {#what-changes}

| Screen | Added in developer mode |
|---|---|
| [Control home](#control-home) | External-control toggle in the `CONTROL INPUT` popover |
| [Motion commands](#motion) | **AI motion** group (learned gaits) and **Position control** group (forced postures) |
| [Gamepad](#gamepad) | Sensitivity, deadzone, button mapping, external control, developer options, diagnostics, wizard |
| [Camera & Vision](#vision) | Camera calibration (the `Vision` popover itself is open to everyone) |
| [Dashboard](#dashboard) | **Robot** and **Vision** tabs; power added to the summary |
| [Settings](#settings) | Enable camera calibration |
| [Connection](#connection) | `Connect by address` card on Android and iOS · `Vision PC IP (optional)` field |
| [Emergency stop](#emergency) | Forced recovery through Position control |
| [Maintenance](#maintenance) | **The entire screen is developer-only** — `Maintenance` tile on the hub |
| Logs | **Nothing** — this screen does not change with the tier |

## Control home {#control-home}

- The **CONTROL INPUT** popover gains the **External control (SLAM/SDK)** toggle, which hands driving over to an
  external program. The `SLAM` chip in the top bar shows while it is on and turns it off again.

→ [Control home](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/control-home.html)

## Motion commands — AI motion · Position control {#motion}

The **Select motion** grid gains an **AI motion** group and a **Position control** group.

**AI motion** holds the learned gaits: `AI Pronk`, `AI Bound`, `AI Pace`, `AI Run`, `AI 2Leg L`,
`AI 2Leg R`, `AI 2Leg F` and `AI 3Leg HL`. They are hidden entirely at the operator level.

**Position control** — `Lock Joints`, `Position Sit` and `Position Stand` — forces a posture without
the normal transitions. The same items are in the long-press list under `SIT`. On wheeled robots the
**Precision·Calib** group also offers `HIGH SPEED`.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Position control changes posture with no trajectory. Use it <strong>only on flat ground with the robot on the floor</strong>. It exists for cases where the normal recovery does not work.</p>
</div>
</div>

→ [Motion commands](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html) · [Emergency stop](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/emergency.html)

## Gamepad {#gamepad}

The following appear in **App settings › Gamepad**.

**Response**

- `Gamepad sensitivity` — input response curve for the physical sticks (separate from the virtual
  joystick setting).
- `Deadzone` — center ignore range, added on top of the device's own dead zone.

**`Button mapping`** — tap a button on the controller diagram to assign a robot motion to it; the
D-pad and stick-center buttons can be mapped too. Mapped buttons are listed under the diagram with an
`×` to remove them. A controller must be connected, and the diagram lights up as you press buttons.

**`External control (SLAM/SDK)`** — hands robot control to an external source. The switch reflects
the robot's real state, so it also updates if another client flips it. The same switch is in the
`CONTROL INPUT` popover on the control home.

**`Developer options`**

| Row | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Send all buttons` | OFF = only L1/R1 reach the robot (the safe default). ON forwards every button, which is what makes chords such as **L1+B** work. It turns on when you enter developer mode and back off when you return to the normal level |
| `One-stick mode` | One-handed operation — swaps only the horizontal axes of the two sticks (vertical stays on each) |
| `Cruise control` | R3 starts cruise, D-pad up/down changes speed. Works only during TROT-family gaits |
| `Publish rate — {hz}Hz` | Joystick frame rate (40 Hz by default). Lower adds latency, higher adds traffic |
| `Input diagnostics` › `Open diagnostics` | The `Gamepad diagnostics` screen — `Connected devices` (name, VID:PID, axes), live `Axes (raw)` bars and a `Button events` key-code log. Use it to check an unknown controller before mapping |
| `Mapping Wizard` › `Start wizard` | Follow the prompts to build a profile for this device — for unknown controllers or when the stick layout is wrong |
| `Delete wizard profile` | Shown only when the connected device has a wizard profile. Deletes it and returns to auto-detection |

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p><code>Send all buttons</code> and <code>Cruise control</code> change how the robot responds to button input. After enabling it, try it in an open area first and stay within reach of <code>E-STOP</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>

→ [Gamepad](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/gamepad.html)

## Camera & Vision {#vision}

![Vision popover](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-vision.pc.en.png)

The `Vision` row on the right card opens the **robot-side vision switches** — that popover is open to
everyone; see [Camera & Vision](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/camera-vision.html). Developer mode adds only the camera
calibration entry at its bottom.

At the bottom of the popover, `Camera calibration` opens the camera calibration tool; the same entry
is under **Robot settings › Calibration › `Open camera calibration`**. Both appear only when camera
calibration is enabled in the app **and** the account is at the developer tier. While a run is in
progress the labels change to `Camera calibration running — tap to cancel` / `Running — tap to cancel`.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>The OAK-D intrinsic calibration makes the robot <strong>walk around by itself for about 10 minutes.</strong> Clear the area before starting it.</p>
</div>
</div>

→ [Camera & Vision](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/camera-vision.html)

## Dashboard {#dashboard}

![Robot state tables](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/dashboard-detail.pc.en.png)

Three tabs appear under the title: **Summary**, **Robot** and **Vision**. The summary also gains
**Power maintenance ▸** (System card).

**Robot** tab tables:

- **Power · PDU** — the title also shows the PDU battery percentage; per rail (**TOTAL**, **BAT L**,
  **BAT R**, **LEGS**, **ADDON**, **EXTERN**, **CHARGE**): voltage, current, temperature and switch
  state. On the CHARGE row the switch column names what is active: **Dock** / **Port**.
- **Device power · 12V/5V** — ON / OFF of each device rail.
- **IMU** — **ANGLE°**, **GYRO (rad/s)**, **ACC (m/s²)** for R(x), P(y), Y(z), with an
  **IMU calibration ▸** shortcut underneath.
- **Joint · JOINT** — one row per joint: **ID**, **STATUS**, **ERR**, **°C B/S** (board / stator),
  **ANGLE°**. STATUS reads *C·H·R* — **C** connected (**N** not), **H** homed, **R** running.
  Green = running and homed, amber = running only, red = otherwise. Temperature turns amber at
  60 °C and red at 70 °C.

**Vision** tab — daemon connection, sensor count, the vision program list with **Vision maintenance ▸**,
and the **Vision sensors** table (STATUS, RGB / IR / 3D fps, EMIT).

→ [Dashboard](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/dashboard.html)

## Settings {#settings}

- **Calibration › `Enable camera calibration`** — turning it on shows `Open camera calibration` below.
  It runs the jig extrinsic / OAK-D intrinsic procedure; progress appears in the top banner.

→ [Settings](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/settings.html)

## Connection {#connection}

On Android and iOS, **Add robot** gains the `Connect by address` card (the web build, the desktop app
and Steam Deck always show it). A collapsed `Vision PC IP (optional)` appears under it, for robots whose
vision computer has its own address. Leave it blank to use the robot IP. It is saved with the robot IP when you connect.

→ [Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html)

## Emergency stop — forced recovery {#emergency}

The `Select motion` grid — opened with the dashed `Motions` button — has a **Position control** group
for cases where the normal recovery does not work. `Lock Joints`, `Position Sit` and `Position Stand` force a posture without a trajectory, so use
them **only on flat ground with the robot on the floor**. The manual joint-by-joint recovery panel is
reserved for internal use.

→ [Emergency stop](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/emergency.html)

## Maintenance — the whole screen {#maintenance}

The **Maintenance** screen is developer-only in its entirety. Without developer mode the
`Maintenance` tile does not appear on the hub, and the route redirects to the control home.

Everything there can **cut the connection, drop the robot or change how its daemons start.**
Read each warning before you press anything.

→ [Maintenance](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/maintenance.html)

# Emergency Stop

::: warning
Always keep the emergency stop button accessible during operation. In any situation where the robot poses a risk to people or property, press the emergency stop button immediately.
:::

## E-STOP in the app

![E-STOP confirmation](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-estop.pc.en.png)

The red `E-STOP` button sits at the right of the top bar on the control home. On the other screens it sits at the right of the header, whenever a robot is connected or is reconnecting after a dropped link — it still works for 8 seconds after the drop. Pressing it opens the confirmation `Emergency stop?`:

> The robot immediately stops all motion and cuts power.
> Reinitialization is required to resume control.

Press `Stop` to send the emergency stop, or `Cancel` to close the dialog. There is no path that fires E-STOP without this confirmation.

- The app sends the emergency stop on a dedicated channel, ahead of anything already queued, and repeats it on the reliable command channel.
- You do not need to own the robot first: the robot accepts E-STOP from any connected device, bypassing the ownership check. It does not take ownership — the current owner stays the same.
- If the robot does not acknowledge the command, the app logs `E-Stop send failed — no response. Use the physical E-Stop`. Do not wait — use the physical button.

## Physical emergency stop button

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/operation/emo.png' alt='Emergency stop button on the rear of the robot' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Emergency stop push button — located on the rear of the robot ]</figcaption>
</figure>

When the physical **emergency stop button** is pressed, or the app's `E-STOP` is confirmed:

- All joints switch to **High Damping** mode.
- The robot resists external motion but does **not** accept torque or position commands.
- The robot may lose its posture and settle to the ground under gravity.

High Damping mode protects both the user and the robot. The robot will not execute any motion commands until the emergency stop is cleared and the robot is re-initialized.

## Recovery

1. **Ensure safety** — confirm that all people and animals are at least 2 m from the robot.
2. **Release the button** — if the physical button was pressed, rotate it clockwise to unlock it.
3. **Return to initial pose** — if the robot has fallen or shifted, place it in the [initial pose](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/initial-pose.html) on a flat surface. Do not force the joints while the robot is in High Damping mode.
4. **Re-initialize** — run the automatic start sequence or the Stand motion from the [control home](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/control-home.html) and confirm the robot state in the top bar before resuming operation.

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#emergency).

## Another controller is in control

Only one client controls the robot at a time. If you are connected while another app or controller holds ownership, the app dims the whole screen after about a second and blocks every control behind the overlay `다른 컨트롤러가 제어 중입니다` (another controller is in control — this overlay is shown in Korean in both languages):

> 보기 전용 — 조작하려면 제어권을 가져오세요 (상대 기기는 보기 전용이 됩니다)
> (View only — take control to operate; the other device becomes view-only.)

A device that is not the owner gets no video, though the status readouts stay visible. The overlay offers:

- `제어권 가져오기` (take control) — asks the robot to hand ownership to this device. The other device becomes view-only, and the overlay disappears once ownership is yours.
- `▶ 자동 기동` — after the confirmation `Run Auto Start?` → `Auto Start`, takes control and runs the automatic start sequence.
- `E-STOP` — after the confirmation `Trigger emergency stop?` → `Run E-STOP`, sends the emergency stop without taking control.

On the control home you can also check and take ownership from the `Overall system status` popover (tap the status chip in the top bar): the `Ownership` row shows `Held` when this device is the owner and `Take ▸` when it is not.

![Overall system status popover with the Ownership row](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-status.pc.en.png)

## Related

- [General Safety Guidelines](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/general-safety-warning-precautions.html)
- [Emergency Stop Procedures (detailed)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/emergency-stop-procedures.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/gamepad.html
================================================================================

# Gamepad

The app drives the robot with the on-screen virtual joysticks by default. Plug in or pair a physical gamepad and the app switches over automatically, with no setup step.

## Automatic detection

- Connect a gamepad over USB or Bluetooth. The app recognizes it immediately, applies a matching profile, and **hides the virtual joysticks**.
- Unplug it and the virtual joysticks come back on their own.
- While a gamepad is active, the only visible change on the control home is that the virtual joysticks are gone. The cards and the viewport stay where they are. The `CONTROL INPUT` popover described below shows a live diagram of the device — its name, sticks, and buttons.

![Control home in gamepad mode — virtual joysticks hidden](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-gamepad.mobile.en.png)

To check what is connected, open **App settings** (the gear button at the top right) › `Gamepad`. The status line reads `Connected` followed by the device name, or `No gamepad connected — using virtual joystick`. Below it, `Active profile:` shows which button/axis layout was picked `(auto-detected)`.

![Gamepad settings](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/settings-gamepad.pc.en.png)

## Choosing the input mode

Two places let you override the automatic choice:

- **App settings › `Gamepad` › `Joystick mode`** — `Auto` / `Virtual joystick` / `Gamepad`. This changes the *UI layout* only; whatever inputs are connected keep working.
- **Control home › `CONTROL INPUT`** (the gamepad button in the tool row outside the left card — just right of the left joystick, or at the left edge with a gamepad) — the same choice as `Auto` / `Virtual` / `Pad`. When a gamepad is connected (and the joystick mode is not set to `Virtual joystick`) this popover also shows a live diagram of what the app is receiving from it.

Leave the mode on `Auto` unless you are troubleshooting.

## Safe button set

Out of the box the app forwards only the two shoulder buttons (**L1 / R1**) to the robot together with the sticks. The app leaves the remaining buttons out of the joystick frame, so an accidental press cannot trigger a robot-side button action. Buttons a developer has mapped in `Button mapping`, and the `Cruise control` keys, still act no matter how this is set.

Entering **developer mode** turns `Send all buttons` on automatically, which forwards every button. Chords the robot reads together with a shoulder button, such as **L1 + B**, need this setting on. While it is off, the other half of the chord never reaches the frame, so nothing happens. Returning to the normal level restores the safe set. The toggle lives in [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#gamepad).

## Typing on a Steam Deck

On a Steam Deck the app draws its own on-screen keyboard: tap any text field and it appears at the bottom of the screen. It types Korean, English, digits and symbols, and the popup you are editing moves up to stay above the keyboard. The field being edited is outlined in blue — there is no blinking cursor, because the keyboard deliberately does not take the focus.

The keyboard can be driven with the gamepad as well:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| D-pad | Move between keys |
| **A** | Press the selected key |
| **B** | Close the keyboard |
| **X** | Backspace |
| **Y** | Space |
| **L1** | Shift |
| **R1** | Switch Korean / English |

`123` and `한` / `A` always show **where the key takes you**, not where you are, and leaving the number layout returns you to the language you used last. `✓` confirms: it presses the popup's own confirm button when there is one, and otherwise submits the field.

While the keyboard is open the gamepad belongs to it — the sticks and buttons do not reach the robot, so the robot cannot move while you pick letters. Other platforms keep using the operating system keyboard.

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#gamepad).

::: warning
`Send all buttons` and `Cruise control` change what the robot does in response to button presses. Test in an open area after turning either on, and keep the E-STOP within reach.
:::

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/introduction.html
================================================================================

# RBQ App

## Downloads {#downloads}

Get the RBQ app from the **[Downloads](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/downloads/)** page — Google Play for Android, the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and an AppImage for Linux desktop and Steam Deck.

## What the app is

The **RBQ app** is the operator application for the RBQ quadruped. Once connected to the robot you can change its posture (sit, stand, walk, stairs and more), drive it with on-screen or physical joysticks, watch the robot's cameras or a 3D view, and check battery, connection and system status.

One app runs on every supported device:

| Platform | Package | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Android tablet / phone | APK | Touch joysticks; a Bluetooth/USB gamepad can be used instead |
| iOS (iPad / iPhone) | App Store / TestFlight build | MFi gamepads are supported |
| Linux desktop | AppImage | Keyboard, mouse and gamepad input |
| Steam Deck | AppImage (Gaming Mode) | Built-in controller is used as the gamepad |

![Control home](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home.pc.en.png)

## The main screens

![The hub](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/hub.pc.en.png)

The app opens on the **Hub**. Its header shows the selected robot's name and connection state on the left — tap the name to open the robot list — followed by the robot battery once connected. At the top right sit the profile button and the gear button for app settings, joined by the red `E-STOP` button while connected.

Every other screen carries the same header with the **logo** and a **Control** button at the top left: the logo returns to the hub, and `Control` goes straight to the control screen.

| Screen | Reach it with | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| **Control** | `Control` button on the hub | Live camera / 3D viewport, motion buttons, joysticks, drive settings — see [Control home](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/control-home.html). Opens once a robot is connected or the sim is running |
| **Dashboard** | `Dashboard` tile | Monitoring cards: system, joints and posture, configuration |
| **Robot settings** | `Robot settings` tile | Calibration, power, payload setup, software update — see [Settings](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/settings.html) |
| **App settings** | Gear button | Gamepad and app settings — see [Settings](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/settings.html) |
| **Logs** | The alert badge in the control top bar, then a row in its list | Real-time robot log, system log and black-box playback |

The `Guide` tile opens this manual. Robots are connected and added from the robot list — see [Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html).

The control screen's top bar comes in two groups. On the left: the **logo**, the status light (tap it for **Overall system status**), the current gait and the signal strength — plus a `SLAM` chip while an external program is driving. On the right: the warning count, the **Robot** battery, your device battery and the red `E-STOP` button.

## Developer mode

The app runs at the **operator tier** by default, and every screen described in this manual is available there. **Developer mode** unlocks additional items intended for customer developers and integrators — extra motions, the **Maintenance** tile on the hub, camera calibration and the external-control toggle on the control home, and a few advanced fields in Settings.

To enable it, open the profile menu (the round button at the top right), turn on the **Developer mode** toggle and enter the
password. The password is issued by Rainbow Robotics and is not printed in this manual.

**What each screen gains, how to turn it on and off, and which actions to be careful with are all
collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html).**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html
================================================================================

# Logs

**Logs** has no menu entry — open it by tapping a red **ERROR** / **FATAL** toast or a row in the alert badge popover on the control home (see [Real Time](#real-time)). Every user can open it. It has three tabs, and the same filter bar works in all of them.

![Real Time tab](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/log-rt.pc.en.png)

## Tabs

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| **Real Time** | Messages streamed from the robot while the app is connected |
| **System Log** | Log files stored on the robot, one per day |
| **Black Box** | Recordings saved when the robot fell, when control was turned off, or when you pressed **Save now** — 30 s of motion data plus the system log of that moment |

A dot next to the tabs shows the log link: **Connected**, **Connecting**, or **Disconnected**.

## Filtering

- **LEVEL** chips — **TRACE**, **DEBUG**, **INFO**, **SUCCESS**, **WARNING**, **ERROR**, **FATAL**. Tap a chip to hide that level; tap again to show it.
- **PROC** chips — one per process in the current source, each in its own color. Tap to hide or show.
- **Search** — filters on the message text or the process name.
- The count at the right of the action bar reads *shown / total* **lines**. Very long files show only the latest 2,500 lines, with a notice at the top.

## Real Time

- **Auto-scroll** — keeps the newest line in view; turn it off to read older lines.
- **Save** — saves the currently filtered lines to your device.
- Tapping a red **ERROR** / **FATAL** toast, or a row in the alert badge popover, opens this tab with that line highlighted so you can see what happened around it.

## System Log

![System Log tab](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/log-sys.pc.en.png)

1. **Fetch** — loads the list of days from the robot (this runs by itself the first time you open the tab, and the newest day is selected).
2. **DATE** — choose a day; the file is loaded and shown with the filters above.
3. **Timeline replay** — plays the day's log as a timeline: play / pause, step to the previous or next line, a position slider, and a speed button that cycles through 0.25× … 16×, 60×, and 300× (the fast speeds skip long quiet stretches). Tapping a line jumps to that moment. **Close** returns to the list.
4. **Save** — saves the raw log file of the selected day to your device.

## Black Box

![Black Box replay](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/log-bb-player.pc.en.png)

1. **Fetch** — loads the list of sessions (this runs by itself the first time you open the tab).
2. **DATE** and **SESSION** — choose a recording; the newest session of the day is opened first and the replay view is shown.
3. **Timeline replay** / **Log list** — toggles between the replay view and the plain log list of that session.
4. **Save now** — asks the robot to record a black-box session right now — use it right after something looked wrong.
5. **Open zip** — replays a session zip saved earlier on this device, without the robot. **Close — to robot session** returns to the robot's list.
6. **Save zip** — saves the selected session (data and log) to your device.

### Replay view

- The header reads **Black Box Playback** with the duration, frame count, and tick. View buttons: **Split** (3D pose + log), **Quad** (data, log, camera, and 3D panes), **3D**, **Data**, **Video** (the event clip on its own), **Logs**.
- The **camera** pane plays the **event clips** (front and rear) for that moment, and playback follows the data timeline. If the robot is still encoding them, the clips may not have arrived yet — try again in a moment. An exported zip carries the clips too, so it replays without the robot.
- **Ref** (top-right of the 3D pane) overlays the reference pose as a translucent ghost so you can compare commanded and measured joints.
- The **Data** pane shows the recorded channels of the current frame. A *miss* chip counts control deadline misses.
- The bottom bar has previous / next frame, play / pause, a slider, the wall-clock time and frame counter, and a speed button cycling 0.25× … 16×.
- The **SYSTEM LOG** pane scrolls in step with the replay position. Tap a line to seek there. A **Time sync uncertain** notice appears when the recording lacks timing metadata or the clocks differ.

## Skimming for errors {#find-errors}

Here is how to pinpoint the moment something went wrong in a whole day of logs, in seconds.

1. In the **LEVEL** chips, press `TRACE`, `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `SUCCESS`, and `WARNING` to **hide** them.
   Only `ERROR` and `FATAL` remain.
2. Press the **next line** button in the timeline replay repeatedly — it steps only between the lines
   that are still shown, so it jumps from error to error.
3. **Write down the timestamp** where you stop (for example `19:30:48.855`).
4. If you need the surrounding context, turn `WARNING` or the relevant **PROC** chips back on there.

When you do not know which process started the problem, skim with every **PROC** chip on, then narrow
to that one process once the range is clear.

## What to send when you contact us {#for-support}

These three together make the cause far quicker to find.

1. **The error messages** — the `ERROR` and `FATAL` list you found with
   [Skimming for errors](#find-errors). Use **Save** to write a file, or capture the screen.
2. **The timestamp** — note when the message appeared.
3. **Video from around that time** — nothing settles it faster than seeing what the robot was doing.

The software version and the steps to reproduce help too. For a momentary problem such as a fall or an
emergency stop, include the **Black Box session** as well, saved with **Save zip**.

**→ [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

## Related

- The battery, joint, and sensor status behind many log messages is on the [Dashboard](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/dashboard.html).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/maintenance.html
================================================================================

# Maintenance

Open `Maintenance` with its tile on the hub; the tile works while the robot is connected. The sections are `Power / System`, `Vision`, `Config file`, and — on robots with an arm — `Arm`.

**This screen is [developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html) only, in its entirety.** Without it the `Maintenance` tile is not shown on the hub and the route redirects to the control home. Everything here can cut the connection, drop the robot or change how its daemons start — read each warning before you press anything.

## Power / System

![Power / System section](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/maintenance-pwr.pc.en.png)

This section exposes every PDU rail, including the ones deliberately kept out of Settings. Toggles show the real rail state from the robot; they are disabled until that state has been received.

**12 V toggles** (one tap): `Speaker amp (12V)`, `LiDAR (12V)`, `CCTV (12V)`, `Thermal (12V)`, `IR LED (12V)`.

**Rails that break the link** (two-step confirmation `Turn this off?` → `Turn off`; the dialog has a `Don't ask for a day` checkbox — once ticked, that rail switches without confirmation for 24 hours on this screen only; Robot settings → Power always confirms):

| Rail | Effect of switching off |
|---|---|
| `Cameras (5V)` | Video stops. |
| `Audio·USB hub (5V)` | Audio devices disappear. |
| `Vision PC (12V)` | Cameras, audio and part of the telemetry on this screen stop. |
| `Comm (12V)` | The app's own connection to the robot is lost. |

**48 V drive rails** (two-step, live voltage shown):

| Rail | Notes |
|---|---|
| `LEGS (48V drive)` | Leg motor power. Can only be switched off while the robot is not standing (sitting, control off or fallen); the row is blocked otherwise. |
| `ARM · ADDON (48V)` | Arm and add-on power — one port for both. Confirm the arm is stopped first. |
| `EXTERN (48V)` | External expansion port power. |

::: danger
Switching `LEGS (48V drive)` off makes the robot collapse. `System reboot` — `Reboot` → `Reboot the robot PC?` → `Reboot` — restarts the robot PC: the robot loses motor power and the app connection drops for the duration. Sit the robot on the floor before either action. The reboot dialog also has the `Don't ask for a day` checkbox.
:::

Below the 48 V rails the section repeats the `Accelerometer calib (ACC)` and `IMU roll/pitch zero` rows described in [Robot settings → Calibration](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/settings.html#calibration); they behave the same here.

## Vision

![Vision section](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/maintenance-vision.pc.en.png)

| Row | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Night mode (Night Vision)` | Switches the IR-cut filter; the CCTV IR-cut and IR LED follow it (switching to day turns the IR LED off). |
| `IR projector` | Depth-camera dot projector, independent of night mode. Shown only on robots that have one. |
| `Stealth mode (LED·buzzer OFF)` | Turns the LEDs and buzzer off together. |
| `GUIDE overlay` | Draws the guide (Aruco cross-hair / box) on the video. |
| `FACE DETECT` | Draws face boxes on the video. |
| `Dock Scan (docking marker)` | Whether the robot detects docking markers in the camera images; the overlay and the `Start docking` button appear when one is found. While docking runs the marker is drawn whatever this says. |
| `Video resolution (SQHD)` | WebRTC encoder output resolution: HD 720p / SQHD 540 / `Eco 360` — lower it on a weak link. |

`IR projector` and `Video resolution (SQHD)` show the state the robot reports. The other toggles show the last value sent to this robot — the app keeps it per robot, so it survives leaving the page or restarting the app, but it can differ after the robot restarts (the note at the bottom of the section says so).

`Heightmap settings` — `Stairs` enables stair terrain recognition; `Edge` enables step-edge detection and is only available while `Stairs` is on.

`Daemon control` — `VISION RESET` → `Reset` has the Handler restart HAL, restarting the camera pipeline cleanly. Video drops for a few seconds; the button shows `Resetting…` and stays unavailable for about 8 seconds.

`Vision Programs` lets you start and stop individual vision daemons by hand (`Vision`, `HAL`, `Streamer`, `Handeye`, `Heightmap`, `Cctv`, `Ptz`, `Thermal`). Their on/off state comes from the robot's reported program status; only on older daemons that do not report it does it fall back to the last command sent.

## Config file

![Config file section](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/maintenance-ini.pc.en.png)

The INI editor edits the robot daemons' configuration files directly. The target selector switches between `Motion.ini`, `HAL · config.ini` and `Handler · config.ini`. Use `Search key` to filter keys; boolean values can be toggled, other values are edited in place. The header shows how many sections were read, when, and `Backup exists` if a backup file is present on the robot.

The footer counts unsaved edits (`{n} changes`). `Revert` discards them, `Reload` re-reads the file from the robot, `Save` opens the confirmation `Save to {label}?` listing every changed key with its old and new value.

::: warning
Saving replaces the **entire** file on the robot with what the editor holds — always edit on top of a freshly loaded file. The previous file is kept as `*_backup.ini`. Changes apply only after the corresponding daemon (Motion, HAL or Handler) is restarted; the app does not restart it for you. Do not change values whose meaning you do not know.
:::

## Arm

Shown only when the robot reports an arm. This section is the initial bring-up.

1. Press `CAN check`, `Release brake`, `Control Start` in that order. Wait for the status badge to light up after each step before pressing the next. ▶ Auto Start ARM runs the whole sequence in one press.
2. `Static poses` sends a fixed pose (`Straight`, `Folding`, `Ready`, `Lift`, `Packing`, `DoorReady`) without a trajectory — on the first use start from `Ready`.
3. `Joint lock / jog` — tap a joint card to lock or unlock it; hold `+` / `−` to jog a locked joint (the buttons are disabled while the joint is unlocked).

RC01 / RC02 attachment sections are not covered by this manual.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html
================================================================================

# Motion commands

Motion commands are sent from the motion card on the left of the [control home](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/control-home.html). A short tap sends the command immediately; the button that matches the robot's current gait is highlighted.

::: danger
Every command here moves the real robot. **Keep people, animals and obstacles at least 2 m away** before pressing, and make sure the robot has completed **Auto Start** and stands on a stable surface.
:::

## Fixed buttons

| Button | What the robot does |
|---|---|
| `SIT` | Folds down into the sitting pose. Joystick input is ignored |
| `STAND` | From sitting: stands up. From walking or stairs: stops and stands in place |
| `WALK` | Starts the walking gait — the joysticks now move the robot |
| `STAIRS` | Stair gait: slower steps with the body leaning to the slope |
| `DOCKING` | Walks onto the charging dock by itself. The button is only there when docking is available — it is not offered on Rapid robots, and it disappears while the `Dock scan` vision toggle is on (the docking overlay on the video takes over) |

Two of the buttons carry a small dot in the corner: **long-press** them to open a sub-list.

- Long-press `SIT` → **Static · Calib**: `ZMP Calibrate` (balance calibration while standing still).
- Long-press `WALK` → **Dynamic Motions**: `Model Walk` (the classic model-based walk), `Wave` and `Run`. `Run` is not offered on wheeled robots.

### Sit

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/eqR7WaP2d-o" title="Sit" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Sit</figcaption>
</figure>

### Stand

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/6QEGjlFkftI" title="Stand" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Stand</figcaption>
</figure>

While standing, the joysticks adjust the posture instead of moving the robot:

| Joystick | Input | Robot action |
|---|---|---|
| L stick | Forward / Backward | Nose up / down |
| L stick | Left / Right | Roll left / right |
| R stick | Forward / Backward | Height up / down |
| R stick | Left / Right | Turn left / right |

### Walk

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/x3d95WWxFF0" title="Walk" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Walk</figcaption>
</figure>

| Joystick | Input | Robot action |
|---|---|---|
| L stick | Forward / Backward | Go forward / backward |
| L stick | Left / Right | Go left / right |
| R stick | Forward / Backward | Pitch forward / backward |
| R stick | Left / Right | Turn left / right |

### Stairs

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dq6S16V7oyE" title="Stairs" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Stairs</figcaption>
</figure>

| Joystick | Input | Robot action |
|---|---|---|
| L stick | Forward / Backward | Go forward / backward |
| L stick | Left / Right | Go left / right |
| R stick | Left / Right | Turn left / right |

::: warning
On stairs and slopes, keep the approach slow and straight. Do not intervene by hand while the robot is adjusting its posture.
:::

## More motions

The dashed **Motions** button at the bottom of the card opens the **Select motion** grid (*Tap to run, then close*). Tapping a tile sends that motion and closes the grid.

![Select motion](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-motion-more.pc.en.png)

`STAIRS` and `DOCKING` are **not** in the grid — they are buttons on the motion card already.

**Model gait**

| Tile | What the robot does |
|---|---|
| `Wave` | Wave gesture |
| `Run` | Faster trot |
| `Model Walk` | Classic model-based walking gait |

**Precision·Calib**

| Tile | What the robot does |
|---|---|
| `ZMP Calibration` | Balance calibration — same as the long-press item under `SIT` |

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#motion).

::: warning Docking
During docking the robot moves on its own. Do not push or steer it, and make sure the dock is placed correctly and powered. The robot stops and starts charging once it is on the dock.
:::

## Drive parameters {#drive-parameters}

Tap **Drive** in the tool buttons next to the left joystick to open the **Drive parameters** popover.

![Drive parameters](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-drive.pc.en.png)

| Control | Range | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `Vision Walk` | on / off | Uses the camera-assisted walking policy while in `WALK`. Switching it while walking changes the policy immediately |
| `Max Speed` | 0.50 – 2.50 m/s | Upper limit of the walking speed the joystick can command |
| `Body Height` | −0.25 – +0.10 m | Standing height offset relative to the default |
| `Body Tilt` | −25° – +25° | Fixed pitch of the body while walking |
| **Reset to default** | — | Restores speed 1.0 m/s, height 0 and tilt 0 |

Slider values are sent to the robot when you release the slider, not while dragging.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2DynPHB6U64" title="Drive parameters" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Drive parameters</figcaption>
</figure>

> **What developer mode adds here** is collected on [Developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html#motion).
