# Battery Handling Precautions

Safe handling, charging, and storage of the RBQ’s on-board battery. For replacement steps, see [Battery Replacement](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/battery.html).

## Charging

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/charging/charging-1.png' alt='Charging with RBQ10 dedicated charger' />
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/charging/description-1.png' alt='Charging with RBQ10 docking station' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Use only the designated charger and docking station. ]</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>1) Charge only with the RBQ10 dedicated charger or RBQ10 docking station. Other chargers can cause overcharge, overheating, or fire.<br>2) While charging, keep the robot and charger away from flammables and heat sources.<br>3) Do not use damaged chargers or cables.</p>
</div>
</div>

Charging steps are described on the [Charging](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/charging.html) page.

- **Fully discharged**: If the robot is fully discharged and will not power on, the docking station may not charge it. In that case, connect the supplied external charger directly to the charging port.

## Handling and storage

- **Impact and penetration**: Do not drop the battery, puncture it, or submerge it. Do not use a damaged battery; contact Rainbow Robotics.
- **Temperature**: Stay within the specified storage and use temperature range. Do not expose to high heat, direct sunlight, or heaters.
- **Storage**: Do not store the battery upside down. If unused for a long time, check its condition periodically.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p><strong>Battery removal when not in use</strong>: When not in use, <strong>remove the battery</strong> for storage. Leaving the battery installed in a powered-off robot for <strong>more than 24 hours</strong> can cause <strong>irreversible damage</strong>.</p>
</div>
</div>

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/electrical-safety.html
================================================================================

# Electrical Safety

Safety rules when working with **electrical equipment** such as the RBQ, chargers, and docking stations.

- **When it applies**: During charging, inspection, and repair; whenever you handle electrical equipment directly.
- **Field use**: In hazardous environments, military use, patrol, etc., ideal electrical conditions may be hard to maintain. Perform charging, internal inspection, and wiring work in a dry, safe place whenever possible.

**High-voltage areas, wet parts, and damaged cables or connectors** pose shock risk. Even if they look intact, **high voltage or strong EMI** can cause latent damage-stop use and inspect if anything seems wrong.

## General precautions

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>Post clear warning signs near electrical equipment where shock is possible.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>1) Do not tear, damage, or remove covers. Be careful when handling labeled parts and nearby components.<br>2) Do not touch internal electrical parts to avoid shock.<br>3) When charging, inspecting, or repairing, do not touch power cables, charging ports, or the controller with wet hands.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Charging and power

- **Designated charger only**: Charge the RBQ10 only with the supplied RBQ10 dedicated charger or docking station. Other chargers risk damage, fire, or shock.
- **Cable check**: Ensure charging and power cables are not tangled or damaged; do not use if damaged.
- **Grounding**: Where you charge or inspect, ensure the controller and docking station are properly grounded per regulations. In field or mobile use, charge in as safe a location as possible.

## Repair and disassembly

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>For internal inspection, part replacement, or cable work, <strong>turn power off</strong> and disconnect the battery if needed.</p>
</div>
</div>

- **No unauthorized modifications**: Do not alter electrical circuits or wiring yourself.

If you have a problem, contact Rainbow Robotics. See [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/emergency-stop-procedures.html
================================================================================

# Emergency Stop Procedures

How to stop the robot immediately in an emergency and how to recover. Routine emergency stop and recovery are also on [Emergency Stop and Recovery](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/emo.html).

## Automatic stop and safety-related behavior

The robot may stop automatically or cut motor power in the following cases:

- **Fall detected**
- **Low battery**
- **Controller (app) stop command** received
- **Interrupt** signal during an automatic mission

The RBQ has **emergency stop (E-Stop)**, **remote stop**, **speed limit**, **posture stabilization**, and other safety-related features. On flat ground, assume a **stopping distance of up to about 1 m** for safety-related stops; on slopes or uneven floors it can be longer.

## Using the emergency stop button

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/operation/emo.png' alt='Emergency stop push button on rear of robot' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Emergency stop push button on the rear of the robot ]</figcaption>
</figure>

Pressing the **emergency stop push button** on the rear puts all joints into **High Damping**. In this state the robot resists external forces but does not accept torque or position commands-control is disabled and the robot may settle to the floor.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>Emergency stop protects people and the robot. Press the button immediately if there is abnormal motion, collision risk, shock, or pinch risk. <strong>It is for real emergencies-not for everyday stopping.</strong> Repeated unnecessary use can add risk by losing controlled stability.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Recovery after emergency stop

1. **Release the button**: Turn the emergency stop button clockwise back to its normal position.
2. **Restore posture**: Run **Auto start** in the app, or set the initial posture per [Robot Initial Pose Setting](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/initial-pose.html).
3. **Find the cause**: Remove or fix the cause of the stop (obstacle, error, wrong settings) before operating again.

## Stop from the app

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home-estop.pc.en.png' alt='The E-STOP button in the app top bar with its confirmation' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ <code>E-STOP</code> at the right of the top bar, with its confirmation ]</figcaption>
</figure>

The red `E-STOP` button sits at the right of the top bar on the control home, and at the right of
the header on the other screens — but only while a robot is connected, or is reconnecting after a
dropped link, where it stays live for 8 seconds. It is not drawn while the app is not connected to a
robot, so in that state reach for **the physical button on the robot** (above). Pressing it opens a
confirmation; the stop is only sent once you press `Stop`. There is no path that skips it.

You do not need robot ownership — the robot accepts an E-STOP from any connected device. The full
behavior is described in [Emergency stop](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/emergency.html).

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p><code>E-STOP</code> cuts power to all motors, so <strong>the robot sags where it stands.</strong> Use it only in critical situations. If the robot does not respond, the app log records <em>E-Stop send failed — no response. Use the physical E-Stop</em> — do not wait, press the physical button.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Residual motion after power off

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>After power is off, RBQ legs <strong>do not auto-lock.</strong> On slopes, stairs, or slippery floors the robot can still slide, roll, or move by inertia-power off does not immediately mean fully safe.</p>
</div>
</div>

On slopes, stairs, or slippery floors after power off you may still get:

- **Sliding**
- **Rolling or falling**
- **Continued motion from inertia**

Before approaching, check floor condition and posture; approach only from a safe direction.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/fire-and-heat-precautions.html
================================================================================

# Fire and Heat Precautions

Measures to prevent fire, burns, and overheating when using the RBQ, charger, and battery.

## Heat and contact

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>1) The robot body and controller get hot after long use. Do not touch during operation or immediately after. Allow at least about 1 hour to cool, check UI temperature, or power off and let it cool.<br>2) Batteries, chargers, and docking stations can also get hot-do not place flammable material near them while charging.</p>
</div>
</div>

- **Ventilation**: Place the controller and charger in a well-ventilated area; do not cover with cloths or covers. Overheating can cause failure or fire.

## Fire prevention

- **Flammables**: Do not place paper, cloth, solvents, or other flammables near the robot or charger.
- **Battery**: Do not expose the battery to fire, crush it, or puncture it. Do not use a damaged battery; dispose of it safely.
- **Charging**: Use only the designated charger; do not use damaged cables or chargers. See also [Battery Handling Precautions](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/battery-handling.html).

## If something goes wrong

- **Smoke or odor**: Turn power off immediately, unplug, and **move to a safe distance**.

<div class="sb sb-danger">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">DANGER</p>
<p><strong>If a fire starts</strong> on the RBQ, charger, or battery, <strong>do not attempt to extinguish it yourself.</strong> Prioritize life safety: <strong>evacuate</strong>, then call the fire service. Lithium batteries are hard to fully extinguish with water or ordinary extinguishers and may worsen the situation-use extinguishers suitable for electrical fires (gas, powder, etc.) as recommended.</p>
</div>
</div>

- **Overheat alarm**: If the product or the app shows an overheat warning, stop use, let it cool, then consult the manual or Rainbow Robotics.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/general-safety-warning-precautions.html
================================================================================

# General Safety Guidelines

General safety rules you must follow when using the RBQ safely. For the meaning of warning symbols, see [Safety Indications](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/indications.html).

## General principles

- The RBQ **can carry payloads** and **supply power to** attachments. Attachments affect stability and energy use depending on weight and shape.
- The RBQ is a **dynamic machine**; **unexpected motion** can occur depending on terrain, floor, and obstacles. If anything seems wrong, stop immediately and check the cause.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>
RBQ motion is dynamic; unexpected behavior can occur depending on terrain, floor condition, and obstacles. If anything seems wrong, trigger emergency stop immediately and find the cause.
</p>
</div>
</div>

## Before operation

- **Trained operators only**: The robot must be operated only by personnel who have read this manual and completed safety training. Read the manual and complete operation and safety training before use.
- **Work area**: Provide **enough clear space** for movement, posture correction, and recovery from falls. Do not leave hazards nearby. In tight or cluttered spaces, correction motions may move the robot in unexpected directions; consider guarding if needed.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/safety/safety-distance.png' alt='Clear work space and guarding' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Provide sufficient work space; install guarding if necessary. ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## During operation

<div class="sb sb-danger">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">DANGER</p>
<p><strong>While the robot is operating, no people, animals (including pets), or other living beings may enter within 2 m of the robot.</strong> Keep that zone clear while the robot is moving and do not touch the robot.</p>
</div>
</div>

- **Emergency stop**: See [Emergency Stop Procedures](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/emergency-stop-procedures.html).
- **No entry**: People and animals (including dogs/pets) must not enter within 2 m of the robot. Do not enter the motion envelope or touch the robot while it is moving.
- **Settings**: Periodically verify installation angle, tool settings, and safety settings.

## Equipment and modifications

- **Safety I/O only**: Connect safety-related equipment only to dedicated safety I/O ports. Do not connect them to general-purpose I/O.
- **No unauthorized modifications**: Do not modify the robot without Rainbow Robotics support. Damage from unauthorized modification is the user’s responsibility.

## Heat and electricity

- **Heat**: The robot and controller can get hot after long use. Touch only after they have cooled.
- **Electrical safety**: See [Electrical Safety](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/electrical-safety.html).

## General warnings

- **Payloads**: Payloads affect stability and energy use. Assess risk by weight and shape before attaching.
- **Obstacles**: Sudden obstacles can cause avoidance or correction that **accelerates in an unexpected direction**. Keep clear space around the robot.
- **Stairs and uneven surfaces**: The robot may change posture abruptly on stairs or uneven floors. Limit speed and approach in those areas.
- **Past performance**: Safe operation in the past does not guarantee the same under the same conditions later. Check the environment and settings regularly.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/handling-and-transportation.html

# Handling and Transportation

Safe handling when moving, packing, and shipping the RBQ. Packing and unpacking steps are also on the [Packing](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/packing.html) page.

## General precautions when moving

- **Power off**: **Always turn power off** before lifting or moving. If power is on, legs can move and cause injury.
- The robot is heavy and joints can move-support it so it cannot fall, or use designated carriers/moving methods.

### Pinch hazard and handles

- Keep **fingers, clothing, long hair, and jewelry** out of handle and joint areas. Grip handles with a **closed fist**; do not insert fingers where they can be pinched.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/safety/handle-1.png' alt='Correct grip on handle with closed fist' style="max-width: 100%; width: min(420px, 100%); display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Grip handles with a closed fist so fingers cannot be pinched. ]</figcaption>
</figure>

### Lifting

- **Two people required**: Always lift with **two people** front and back. **With one hand support the left/right legs (or body side)**; **with the other hand grip the handle in a fist**. **Lift using the handle** so the whole robot stays level and stable. Lifting from one side only or twisting can drop legs or shift the center of mass.
- The RBQ is **modular**. Unlike a single-piece body, **parts can separate and fall** more easily. Avoid shock and twisting when lifting; do not drop-coordinate and move slowly.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/safety/handle-2.png' alt='Two-person lift front and back' style="max-width: 100%; width: min(420px, 100%); display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ One hand supports left/right legs; the other grips the handle-lift by the handle and move the whole robot steadily. ]</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>Do not force-lift or drag while power is on. Turn power off and secure a stable posture first. Modular construction is more vulnerable to separation and drops than a one-piece design-take extra care against shock and drops.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Packing and shipping

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/packing/packing-8.png' alt='Robot packed and secured in box' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Ship in original packaging and secure so nothing moves inside the box. ]</figcaption>
</figure>

- **Original packaging**: Use the factory packaging when possible-shock and vibration can damage internal parts.
- **Securing**: Cushion and secure so the robot cannot move inside the box.
- **Labeling**: Mark handling (orientation, fragile, etc.) and avoid excessive stacking or throwing.

## Battery

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>For air or sea shipment with the battery installed, check applicable rules (e.g. UN dangerous goods, airline rules). If required, remove the battery and ship separately-confirm in the manual or with Rainbow Robotics.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Docking station and charger

- **Charger and docking station**: Pack and ship without shock; avoid tangling or crushing cables.

## Storage

- **When not in use**: Store in the **dedicated case** or **docking station** when possible. Case size and weight are in the product documentation.
- **Environment**: Follow **storage temperature and humidity** in [Operating Environment Requirements](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/operating-environment-requirements.html). For the battery, follow [Battery Handling Precautions](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/battery-handling.html).

# Maintenance Safety

Safety rules for maintenance such as battery replacement, foot/bumper/leg module replacement, and calibration.

## Before work

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>1) Before maintenance, turn robot power off and disconnect the battery if needed.<br>2) Touch parts only after the robot has fully stopped. Confirm joints are in a safe state.<br>3) Use only specified tools and procedures. Disassembly or assembly not in the manual can cause damage or injury.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Battery and electrical

- **Battery replacement**: Follow [Battery Handling Precautions](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/battery-handling.html) and [Battery Replacement](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/battery.html).
- **Cables and connectors**: When [detaching connectors](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/connector.html), do not pull on cables-use the specified method.

## Mechanical parts

- **Legs, feet, bumper**: When replacing [feet](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/foot.html), [leg modules](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/leg-module.html), or [stand and bumper](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/bumper.html), confirm screws and fasteners are tight-loose parts can come off during operation.
- **Calibration**: Perform [calibration and tuning](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/calibration-tuning.html) per the manual and the app only when the robot is stable.

## Work environment

- **Flat surface**: Work on a level, stable surface-the robot can fall on a slope.
- **Solo heavy lifting**: When lifting heavy parts alone, get help or use equipment to avoid injury.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/safety/initial-pose.png' alt='Maintenance on a flat stable surface' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Perform maintenance on a level, stable surface. ]</figcaption>
</figure>

If unsure or something is wrong, contact Rainbow Robotics. See [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/).

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/mechanical-safety.html

# Mechanical Safety

Measures to prevent injury or damage from joints, legs, and drive components.

## Motion envelope and access

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/safety/warning.png' alt='Joint and leg motion range; pinch hazard' style="max-width: 100%; width: min(420px, 100%); display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ During motion, keep hands, clothing, and cables clear of joints and legs. ]</figcaption>
</figure>

**Red circles** in the figure mark **hazard zones** with pinch and collision risk (around hip and leg joints). During handling, transport, and inspection, do not put fingers, clothing, cables, long hair, or jewelry into these zones.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>1) Do not enter the motion envelope or put hands or body on the robot body or legs while it is moving-risk of pinch and collision.<br>2) If the robot falls or corrects posture, people or objects nearby can be struck-maintain sufficient clear space.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Locomotion and speed

- **Walking**: The RBQ moves on four legs. Observe **speed, acceleration, and load limits** in the manual and the app. Speed changes take effect immediately; actual speed depends on floor friction, commands, balance correction, and faults.
- **Stay within limits**: Overload or excessive speed can cause failure or unstable motion. Collisions with objects can release large kinetic energy-apply safety settings suited to the environment.

## Joints, legs, and pinch risk

- **Pinch points**: Mainly around **hip** and **leg joints**. During normal driving, hands usually cannot reach them, but during **handling, transport, and inspection**, keep fingers, clothing, cables, hair, and jewelry clear.
- **If something is wrong**: Stop immediately, trigger emergency stop, find the cause, then continue.

## Stairs, slopes, and uneven floors

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>On stairs or uneven surfaces the robot will try to adjust posture; you cannot eliminate all errors. Do <strong>not</strong> use sudden manual intervention or force the robot to stop. Limit approach distance and speed on stairs and slopes; keep about 2 m clearance if needed.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Installation and movement

- **Flat floor**: Use the robot on a flat, stable floor per specifications. It can fall on slopes or slippery surfaces.
- **Handling and transport**: Follow the procedures for moving, packing, and shipping. See [Handling and Transportation](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/handling-and-transportation.html).

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/operating-environment-requirements.html
================================================================================

# Operating Environment Requirements

The RBQ is a quadruped robot used in **various environments**-indoors, general workshops, hazardous sites, military use, patrol/inspection, etc.

- **Below**: Recommended conditions for general use and specification limits.
- **Special environments** (hazardous workplaces, military, unmanned patrol, etc.) may require separate risk assessments and additional measures.

## Recommended environment (general use)

The following are recommended for normal operation and service life. Performance and warranty apply when these are met.

### Temperature and humidity

- **Operating temperature**: **-20 to +43 °C** (see [General Specifications](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/product-descriptions/general-specification.html)). Outside this range you may get reduced performance, failure, or shorter battery life.
- **Humidity**: In very damp or condensing environments, sensors and electrical parts can be affected-use and store within the specified humidity range when possible.

### Floor and space

- **Flatness**: The robot is most stable on flat, solid floors within the specified limits. On steep slopes, rough terrain, or slippery surfaces it may fall or become unstable.
- **Space**: Provide enough room for movement, posture correction, and recovery from falls. **While operating, no people or animals (including pets) may enter within 2 m of the robot.** Keep safe clearance from obstacles as well.

### Electromagnetic and physical environment

- **Magnetic fields**: Strong fields can affect sensors and control-avoid use when possible.
- **Vibration and shock**: Excessive vibration or shock can cause failure or bad measurements-damp or isolate, or limit use.

### Hazardous environments

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Do not use in explosive atmospheres, flammable gas, or heavy dust. If no IP rating is stated, <strong>do not use</strong> outdoors, in rain, or near water features (use is prohibited).</p>
</div>
</div>

## Use in special or marginal environments

In hazardous workplaces, military use, unmanned patrol, disaster sites, or hard-to-access inspections, **temperature, humidity, floor, and space** may not meet specification, and unpredictable hazards may exist.  
If you use the RBQ for such purposes, perform a **risk assessment before use** and apply **additional safety devices, procedures, and PPE** as needed. Warranty may not apply to failures or damage from use outside the specified environment.

Contact Rainbow Robotics if needed. See [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/user-responsibility-disclaimer.html
================================================================================

# User Responsibility Disclaimer

Scope of responsibility and limitations when using the RBQ and related manuals and software.

<div class="sb sb-required">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-book" aria-hidden="true">📖</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">REQUIRED READING</p>
<p>You must read the user manual and safety-related documentation. Review these documents in advance for legal and safety responsibility.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Intended use and prohibited use

### Intended use

- The RBQ is a quadruped robot intended for **transport and movement** in **industrial sites, restricted areas, and supervised environments**.
- Use is assumed in **designated or marked areas**. See [Operating Environment Requirements](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/operating-environment-requirements.html) and [Specifications](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/hardware/specification.html) for motion and environment limits.
- You may mount **non-contact sensing and monitoring payloads**; power can be supplied to such payloads.

### Unsuitable use

- The RBQ is **not suitable for collaborative work** where people and the robot share the same space continuously.
- Use outside the intended scope without a risk assessment is prohibited.

### Explicit prohibitions

The following uses are prohibited (examples only; not exhaustive):

- **No riding**: Carrying or transporting people or animals
- Underwater or airborne use; weapon or medical device use; home use; transport of hazardous materials; intentional harm; illegal purposes; climbing assistance; tampering that impairs sensors or function, etc.

**Low-level API control of joints** is outside the intended use described in this document. If you use it that way, you need a **separate risk assessment**. See the [Developer Guide](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/developers-guide.html) and API documentation.

## Lawful use

- The user is responsible for complying with all applicable laws and regulations.
- The product must be used only within the purposes, environments, and limits specified in the manual and by Rainbow Robotics. Rainbow Robotics is not liable for damage from use outside those limits.

## Safety and risk

- **Risk assessment**: The user or system integrator must perform a risk assessment for the actual environment (workplace, coexistence with people and equipment, etc.). Configure guards, devices, and procedures accordingly.
- **Training**: Anyone who operates, inspects, or maintains the system must complete the relevant manual and safety training before use.

## Modifications and unauthorized repair

- If you modify the product or change parts or software without Rainbow Robotics approval, Rainbow Robotics is not liable for failures, accidents, or damage that result.
- Repair and inspection should be within what the manual allows the user to do, or contact Rainbow Robotics. See [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/).

## Improper use

- Improper use (explosive atmospheres, medical/life-related uses, transport of people or animals, no risk assessment, use beyond specifications, etc.) is prohibited. Rainbow Robotics is not liable for direct or indirect damage from such use.

For legal or safety questions about product use, contact Rainbow Robotics. See [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/).
