# Requesting support (C/S · A/S)

How to file a request with Rainbow Robotics' official support desks. The page runs in order:
**check it yourself → what to prepare → how to produce logs → where to send it.** The submission
links are at the **[bottom](#where-to-send)** — a request that arrives complete is resolved far
faster than one that starts a round of questions.

::: danger ⚠ If safety is involved, stop first
Fire, smoke, abnormal motion or risk of injury — carry out
[Emergency stop and recovery](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/guides/common/emo.html) before reading any further.
:::

## 1. Check it yourself first {#before-you-ask}

Many symptoms already have an answer. Five minutes covers it.

- [Troubleshooting by symptom](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/joystick-not-working.html) — joystick not
  responding, no camera view, docking retries, and so on
- [Dashboard](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/dashboard.html) — battery voltage and the `IMU`, `CAN`, `FindPose`,
  `Control` health
- [Logs and Black Box](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html) — what error appeared at that moment

None of that effort is wasted: **write what you checked into the "already tried" section of the
request below.**

### Ask the AI first {#ask-ai}

This documentation site has a button that opens **an AI grounded in the complete manual**.
Press **`Ask AI`** at the left of the top bar — it is on every page.

| What it does | Prepares a question that points the assistant at the full manual (`llms-full.txt`) and opens it in **Claude** or **ChatGPT** |
| --- | --- |
| Your options | `Open in Claude` · `Open in ChatGPT` · `Copy prompt for AI` (to paste into another assistant) |
| Cost | You need an account with that AI service |

**It suits questions like** — "what is the center of mass measured from?", "what is the difference
between STAIRS mode and the Stairs motion?", "what does this setting change?" — anything **the
manual already answers**. It is especially quick when the answer is spread across several pages.

::: warning ⚠ Do not take AI answers at face value
An AI can state **a wrong answer convincingly**. Always confirm the following against the manual
itself or with support:

- **Safety and maintenance procedures** — emergency stop, battery handling, disassembly
- **Anything that actually moves the robot** — read the source page before entering values
- **Fault diagnosis** — the AI cannot see your robot. File real faults through the steps below
- **Recent changes** — it does not know what has not reached the documentation yet
:::

## 2. What goes into the request {#how-to-fill}

The CS and A/S forms use the same fields.

### Product details {#product-info}

| Field | What to enter | Where to find it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Product type** | `RBQ Series` | — |
| **Product name** | `RBQ10` | — |
| **Serial number** | The robot's unique number | Under the robot's name in the hub's robot list and in the `Robot settings` title, or the label on the robot |
| **Installation date** | `YYYY.MM.DD` | Delivery / installation record |
| **Region** | Where the robot is | — |
| **Seller** | The dealer or contact you bought from | Purchase record |
| **Software in use** | `Yes` / `No` | `Yes` if you drive the robot from the SDK or your own program |

::: tip 📝 Finding the serial number in the app
**Dashboard** → the `Robot S/N` row at the top of the **System** card. The robot reports it, so it
is read-only, and it only appears while connected. It is also under the robot's name in the hub's
robot list and in the `Robot settings` title.
:::

### The payload you have fitted {#payload}

**Always state what is mounted on the robot.** Unstable walking and repeated falls most often come
from payload mass and center-of-mass values that do not match reality. Without this, it is the
first thing support has to ask for.

Three things to write down:

| Item | Example |
| --- | --- |
| **What is fitted** | PTZ camera, Livox LiDAR ×2, LTE/5G module |
| **Values entered in the app** | Mounted slots `5 / 13` · total mass `7.19 kg` · CoM `(-0.006, 0, 0.173) m` |
| **Do they match the hardware** | Whether you measured them, or left the defaults |

#### Where to read the values {#where-to-read-payload}

**Robot settings › Payload setup** shows which of the 13 slots are ticked and what each one holds. The
**total** under the list is the overall mass and center of mass.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/settings-robot.pc.en.png' alt='Robot settings › Payload setup — slots and total' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Capture the ticked slots with their values, plus the total below ]</figcaption>
</figure>

The **Dashboard › Config** card summarizes the same values — `Mounted slots`, `Total mass` and
`CoM X · Y · Z`. Either way, **a screenshot carries all of it** with no transcription.

::: warning ⚠ Check nothing is still ticked after removing a load
Removing equipment means unticking its slot as well. A slot left ticked makes the robot account for
mass that is not there, and walking becomes unstable — a genuinely common cause.
Entering values is covered in
[Robot settings › Payload setup](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/settings.html#robot-parameters).
:::

If you have just fitted or changed a payload, **say whether you ran the ZMP calibration**
([ZMP Calibration](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/guides/add-on/zmp-calibration.html)). If not, doing that first may be the quicker
route.

### Writing the description {#inquiry-content}

**"It doesn't work" guarantees one extra round of email.** Filling in the blocks below usually gets
the cause narrowed down in the first reply. Copy the template as-is.

```text
[Symptom]
One line on what happens. (e.g. Switching to WALK, the robot collapses after 3 seconds)

[How to reproduce]
1. Robot on level ground, auto start completed
2. STAND → WALK
3. Push the left joystick forward; it collapses ~3 s later

[When and how often]
Since around 2026-09-01 14:30. 8 times out of 10.

[Software versions]
App: 1.2609.0   Robot: 1.2609.0   (Robot settings › Software update)

[Payload fitted]
PTZ camera + Livox LiDAR ×2 + LTE/5G · slots 5/13 · 7.19 kg total
CoM (-0.006, 0, 0.173) m · measured values entered · ZMP calibration done

[Already tried]
- Rebooted the robot → unchanged
- Re-entered payload values → unchanged
- Ran the manual's "If the robot falls" procedure → recovers, but recurs
```

The **two version numbers (app and robot)** are the ones most often left out, and a mismatch
between them genuinely causes symptoms — it is the first thing support checks. Copy the `Version`
values of `This app (GUI)` and `Current robot` straight from **Robot settings › Software update**.

### Attachments {#attachments}

The form takes **one** file, and only certain formats.

| Accepted | `.jpg` · `.jpeg` · `.png` · `.pdf` · `.zip` |
| --- | --- |

::: warning ⚠ Log files cannot be uploaded as-is
`.log`, `.txt` and `.csv` are rejected. **Wrap them in a `.zip`.** Put everything in one zip when
you have more than one file to send.
:::

What is worth attaching, in order of usefulness:

1. **The Black Box zip** — attitude and numeric recording from around the incident. The single most
   useful attachment.
2. **A screenshot of the payload configuration** — see
   [Where to read the values](#where-to-read-payload).
3. **A screenshot showing the symptom** — the error message, or abnormal values on the Dashboard.
4. **Video** — if it is large, host it and put the link in the description instead.

### Contact details and consent {#contact}

| Field | Note |
| --- | --- |
| Company · department · name | — |
| Phone | — |
| Email | **This is where the reply goes.** A typo means no answer |
| How you found us | Search · News · Exhibition · SNS · Referral · Other |
| Privacy consent | **Required — the form will not submit without it** |

## 3. Producing the logs to attach {#collect-logs}

Logs come from the **Logs** screen of the **RBQ app**. It has no menu entry — open it by tapping a
red **ERROR** / **FATAL** toast, or a row in the alert badge popover in the control home's top bar.
The screen itself is documented in [Logs and Black Box](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html).

### Black Box zip — do this first {#blackbox-zip}

For anything momentary — a fall, a fault — this one file is the most useful thing you can send. It
carries the attitude, voltage and joint values from that instant alongside the log.

1. Open **Log → Black Box**.
2. Choose the date and time window under **DATE** and **SESSION**.
3. Press **Fetch** to load the recording.
4. Scrub the transport bar to confirm **it is the right window**.
5. Press **Save zip** — attach that file as it is.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/log-bb-player.pc.en.png' alt='Black Box replay screen' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Black Box — choose DATE and SESSION, then Save zip ]</figcaption>
</figure>

### System log {#system-log}

Use this to send past logs by date.

1. In **Log → System Log**, pick a day under **DATE** and press **Fetch**.
2. Leaving only **`WARNING`, `ERROR` and `FATAL`** in the level filter cuts the noise sharply.
3. Press **Save** to download the file.
4. **Zip the downloaded file** before attaching it.

### Screenshot {#screenshot}

If you can make the symptom happen again, this is the quickest route.

1. Open **Log → Real Time**.
2. **Reproduce** the symptom once.
3. **Screenshot** the messages that appeared at that moment. Narrowing the level and process
   filters first makes it much easier to read.

::: tip 📝 When it will not reproduce
Pick the day in **System Log** and capture around the time it happened. If you do not know the
exact time, the rough window is enough.
:::

### Bundling several files {#zip-together}

Only one attachment is accepted, so combine them.

```bash
# Linux · macOS — after gathering the files in one folder
zip -r rbq-support-2026-09-01.zip folder-to-send/
```

On Windows, right-click the folder and choose **Compress to ZIP file**. Putting the **date and
serial number** in the filename makes it easier for support to find later.

## 4. Filing it {#where-to-send}

With everything prepared, choose the desk below. There are two, and **picking the wrong one delays
the reply** while it is handed to the right team.

| Situation | Desk |
| --- | --- |
| A question about usage, features, settings or specifications | **[File a CS support request](https://rainbow-robotics.com/en/customer-support/technical-support/cs-support/)** |
| A fault or error that needs **inspection or repair** | **[File an A/S support request](https://rainbow-robotics.com/en/customer-support/technical-support/as-support/)** |

The dividing line is simple — **if the robot has to be shipped or someone has to visit, it is A/S**;
if an answer settles it, it is CS. When in doubt, file with CS; it gets routed internally.

There are developer-facing channels as well.

| Channel | For |
| --- | --- |
| [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/RainbowRobotics/RBQ/issues) | Reproducible software bugs |
| [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/RainbowRobotics/RBQ/discussions) | Questions and feature requests |
| [rbq.support@rainbow-robotics.com](mailto:rbq.support@rainbow-robotics.com) | Private, business or licensing matters |

## 5. After filing {#after}

- The reply goes to **the email address you entered**. Check the spam folder too.
- Reply **in the same email thread** when following up. Filing again splits the history.
- If more logs are requested, repeat [Producing the logs to attach](#collect-logs) and send them.
- If the robot has to be shipped, follow the [Packing](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/guides/common/packing.html) procedure.

## See also {#see-also}

- [Contact us](https://rainbow-robotics.com/en/customer-support/contact-us/) — sales and support contacts
- [Resources](https://rainbow-robotics.com/en/customer-support/resources/) — catalogues and documents
- [Downloads](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/downloads/) — app, robot software, CAD, manual PDFs

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/battery-one-side.html
================================================================================

# Battery drains on one side

## Check each pack on its own {#single-pack-check}

To find out whether one pack is faulty, fit **one pack at a time** and check whether the robot powers on.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p><strong>Never stand the robot up or walk it with only one battery pack fitted.</strong> The only thing this check confirms is <strong>whether the robot powers on</strong>. Switch the power off again as soon as you have confirmed it.</p>
</div>
</div>

1. Put the robot in a **sitting posture** and switch the power off.
2. Fit **one battery pack only**.
3. Switch the power on and confirm **only that the robot powers up**.
4. Switch the power off and remove the pack.
5. Fit **the other pack only** and repeat step 3.

See [Battery replacement](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/battery.html) for how to remove and refit the packs.

### Interpreting the result {#result}

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Both power on | Both packs are supplying power correctly |
| Only one powers on | The pack that does not power on, or its connector, has a problem |
| Neither powers on | The cause is something other than the batteries |

## When the two packs differ significantly in voltage {#voltage-imbalance}

A large voltage gap between the two packs can cause problems.
If only one pack powers the robot in the check above, or the symptom returns after swapping
packs, stop operating the robot and [contact us](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/).

## Still stuck? {#still-stuck}

Tell us the result of the check — whether each pack powered the robot on. [Contact us](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)

For handling precautions, see [Battery Handling Precautions](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/safety/battery-handling.html).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/calibration-tuning.html
================================================================================

# Calibration and tuning

The calibrations that keep the robot walking steadily are collected under **Robot settings → Calibration**
in the app.

![Robot settings → Calibration](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/settings-cal.pc.en.png)

## ZMP calibration

ZMP (Zero Moment Point) calibration **finds the center-of-mass offset automatically while the robot
stands.** Run it after changing the load, or when the walk drifts to one side.

### Before you start

- Put the robot on **flat, firm ground**.
- Leave **room for the robot to take one step** — it aligns its legs with a step before calibrating.
- The app must be connected to the robot.
- **The robot must be standing.** It cannot start while sitting or with control off.

### Procedure

1. Open **Robot settings → Calibration** in the app.
2. Under **ZMP Calibration**, press `Auto-calibrate ZMP offset`. If the robot is not in a state where
   it can run, the button is locked and **the reason is shown right there** (for example *The robot
   must be standing — ZMP calibration cannot start while sitting or with control off*).
3. Confirm in the dialog.
4. The robot **takes one slow step to square up its legs**, then starts calibrating. The progress
   window shows *Calibrating the ZMP offset…* and it takes **up to 60 seconds**.
5. On convergence the robot **saves the value itself and returns to STAND.** The window shows
   *ZMP calibration complete.* and closes after two seconds.
6. Move the robot around and confirm it behaves normally.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p><strong>Do not touch the robot</strong> until the calibration finishes. Putting anything on it or pushing it throws the calibration off. Closing the window does not stop it — the robot keeps calibrating.</p>
</div>
</div>

### If it fails

A failure **leaves the previous calibration in place.** Act on the reason shown in the window.

| Message on screen | What to do |
|---|---|
| *The robot must be standing.* | Switch to STAND and run it again |
| *Wait until the robot is completely still, then run it again.* | Wait for walking or turning to stop |
| *Place the robot on level ground.* | The ground is sloped — move to a flat surface |
| *The alignment step did not finish.* | Clear room for one step and run it again |
| *It did not converge within 60 s.* | Check that the floor is not soft or slippery, then run it again |
| *The robot is not responding.* | Check the [connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html) |

The reason is also written to the system log — see [Logs](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html).

## Related

- If you changed the load, **update the [payload configuration](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/payload_setting.html)
  first**, then calibrate. The other order leaves the calibration tied to the old load.
- The **IMU zero**, **leg home pose (jig)**, **camera** and **docking** calibrations on the same
  screen are described in [Settings](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/settings.html).

## Still stuck {#still-stuck}

Tell us which calibration failed, the reason shown on screen, and what was loaded on the robot at the time.

**→ [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/docking-retry.html
================================================================================

# Docking keeps retrying

The robot fails to dock at the charging station and keeps trying again. In most cases
**the marker is not visible**; the next most common cause is **an alignment offset**.

## First checks {#first-checks}

- Confirm the robot is **within 3 m** of the docking station.
- Confirm the robot's **front or rear camera is facing the docking station**.
- Check the marker on the docking station for obstructions, dirt or water.
- Confirm the docking station is powered.

## The marker is not recognized {#marker-not-found}

**Cause:** Docking works by locating the marker on the docking station. Recognition fails if
any of the following applies.

- The distance is **more than 3 m**.
- Only part of the marker is visible. The marker is a group of several patterns on one board, and **enough of them must be fully visible** for the pose to be computed.
- The marker is hard to see because of shade, backlight or reflections.

**Fix:**

1. Move the robot **within 3 m, in front of** the docking station.
2. Clean the marker surface and remove anything blocking it.
3. If there is direct sunlight or strong reflection, change the lighting or move the station.
4. Start docking again.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>Do not move the robot by hand while docking. The docking station must also be fixed to the floor.</p>
</div>
</div>

## The marker is recognized but the alignment is off {#alignment-off}

**Cause:** The robot reaches the front of the docking station but is slightly out of position
laterally or front-to-back. The alignment offsets need adjusting.

**Fix:** Adjust `Offset X` and `Offset Y` following
[Adjusting the docking parameters](#dock-parameters) below.

## Adjusting the docking parameters {#dock-parameters}

The alignment offsets and retry counts can be viewed and changed under
**Robot settings → Calibration → Docking calibration** in the app.

### Preparation {#preparation}

- Move the robot to a place where docking can be tested.
- Keep the surrounding area clear of obstacles.
- The app must be connected to the robot.

### Procedure {#procedure}

1. Open **Robot settings → Calibration** in the app and scroll down to **Docking calibration**. The current
   values load automatically when you enter the screen; press `Reload` to read them again.
2. Edit the values that are off.
3. Press `Apply` to store them on the robot. The screen refreshes with the values the robot actually
   accepted and shows *Applied (re-confirmed with robot values)*.
4. Repeat steps **2–3** until docking is stable.
5. Once adjusted, use the docking function as usual.

To restore the originals press `Defaults` — it only fills the fields with the factory values, so
**you still have to press `Apply` to store them on the robot.**

### Adjustable parameters {#parameters}

| Item | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `Offset X (m)` | Position correction along the robot's X axis | — |
| `Offset Y (m)` | Position correction along the robot's Y axis | — |
| `Req Count` | Upper limit on consecutive failed responses when requesting the marker (charger) pose | 300 |
| `Try Count` | How many times docking is retried after a failure | 10 |

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Raising the retry counts is not a real fix. If the marker cannot be seen, a higher count only repeats the failure for longer. Check the recognition conditions above first.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Still stuck? {#still-stuck}

Open **[Logs → Real Time](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html#real-time)**, start docking and read the messages that appear.
Phrases such as `Marker Not Found` or `too far` are useful to include.

See [Charging](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/charging.html) for docking station installation requirements.

**→ [Contact us](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/joystick-not-working.html
================================================================================

# Joystick does nothing

Buttons such as sit and stand work, but moving the sticks does not move the robot. Usually either
**control is held elsewhere**, or the app never picked up the gamepad.

## First checks {#first-checks}

Open **App settings → Gamepad**. The status line at the top says exactly where you are.

![Gamepad settings](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/settings-gamepad.pc.en.png)

| Status line | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `Connected` + device name | The pad is being read | Go to [Ownership](#ownership) below |
| `No gamepad connected — using virtual joystick` | The pad was not picked up | See [Pad not detected](#not-detected) below |

If `Active profile:` names the wrong device, the stick layout is off and controls behave oddly — build
a profile for your device with the `Mapping Wizard` in **App settings → Gamepad** ([developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html) required).

## The pad is not detected {#not-detected}

- **Press a button once.** For privacy reasons, browser and desktop builds **only expose a device
  after a button press**. Moving the sticks is not enough — this is the most common false alarm.
- **Reconnect over USB or Bluetooth.** On connection the app picks the device up immediately and
  hides the virtual joysticks.
- **Check the joystick mode.** With `Joystick mode` set to `Virtual joystick`, the
  screen keeps the virtual sticks even with a pad attached. Set it back to `Auto`. The same choice is
  in the `CONTROL INPUT` popover on the left card of the control home.
- **Steam Deck** must be launched in **gaming mode** (or through the Steam client) for the built-in
  pad to be visible to the app. Launched directly from desktop mode, the pad is emulated as mouse and
  keyboard and the app never sees it.

## The on-screen input moves but the robot does not {#ownership}

**Cause:** Another device holds ownership. The robot accepts input from one device at a time.

**Fix:** When another device holds it, after about a second the app covers the screen with the
`다른 컨트롤러가 제어 중입니다` overlay (another controller is in control) — press
**`제어권 가져오기`** (take control) to take it over. If no overlay appeared, tap the status chip in
the top bar and look at the **Ownership** row of **Overall system status**: `Take ▸` means this
device is not the owner.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>With <code>External control (SLAM/SDK)</code> enabled in <strong>App settings → Gamepad</strong>, the robot follows an external program and ignores joystick input. The status chip in the top bar then shows <code>SLAM</code>. (The setting is visible in <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html">developer mode</a> only.)</p>
</div>
</div>

## The robot stops mid-manoeuvre {#input-timeout}

**Cause:** If no joystick input arrives for **more than one second**, the robot zeroes every control
input as a safety measure. A brief wireless dropout stops the robot where it stands.

**Fix:** Move closer to the robot and keep metal structures and walls out of the path.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>This is a safety feature, not a fault. It exists so the robot does not keep moving after the control signal is lost.</p>
</div>
</div>

## The sticks work but the buttons do not {#buttons}

By default the app forwards only the sticks and **L1 · R1** to the robot. The other buttons are left
out on purpose so a stray press cannot trigger a robot action — this is not a fault.

To attach actions to buttons, use `Button mapping` in **App settings → Gamepad**, or enable
`Send all buttons` in [developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html). See [Gamepad](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/gamepad.html) for the details.

## It only fails in stair mode {#stair-mode}

**Cause:** Stair mode runs on camera data. With no camera image, the joystick can appear dead.

**Fix:** First check that the video is coming through — see
[No camera view](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/no-camera-view.html).

If the video is fine and only stair mode fails, see
[Stair mode does not move](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/stair-mode-not-moving.html).

## Still stuck {#still-stuck}

Check whether anything appears in **[Logs → Real Time](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html#real-time)** while you
operate, and tell us what the status line in **App settings → Gamepad** said.

**→ [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/no-camera-view.html
================================================================================

# No camera view

The robot is connected, but no camera video appears in the app. Work through the steps below.

## 1. Check which source you are on {#source}

If the viewport is on `3D`, it shows the robot's 3D pose rather than video — that is not a fault.

![The viewport and its source name](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/home.pc.en.png)

Tap the **source name above the center of the viewport** to open the list and pick a camera source
such as `Front`. The list contains **only the cameras the robot actually reports**, so if the source
you want is missing, that camera is not reaching the robot — go to step 2.

Which devices each source needs is listed in [Camera & Vision](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/camera-vision.html).

## 2. Check the vision status {#vision-status}

Open the **Dashboard** and go to the **Vision** tab — it is only visible in [developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html).

![Dashboard vision tab](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/dashboard-vision.pc.en.png)

- Look at **daemon connection** and **sensor count** first. With no daemon attached the whole video
  path is down.
- In the **Vision sensors** table, check each sensor's `STATUS` and `RGB / IR / 3D fps`. An fps of 0
  means no frames are coming from that sensor.

To start and stop the vision programs by hand, use `Vision Programs` under **Maintenance → Vision**
(see [Maintenance](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/maintenance.html)).

## 3. Check camera power {#power}

A camera with no power appears in neither the list nor the video.

![Maintenance power screen](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/maintenance-pwr.pc.en.png)

Under **Maintenance → Power / System**, check that these are on.

| Item | What it cuts |
|---|---|
| `Cameras (5V)` | The body vision cameras — turning it off stops the video |
| `Vision PC (12V)` | The vision PC — cuts the cameras, audio and part of the telemetry on this screen |
| `CCTV (12V)` · `Thermal (12V)` | The color and thermal cameras of the PTZ unit |

## 4. Try a lower resolution {#resolution}

On a weak wireless link the video may not come up at all. Tap the **resolution tile** on the
**Observation** card at the right and drop to `SQHD 540` or `Economy 360`.

## 5. Reconnect {#reconnect}

If everything above is fine and there is still no video, make the connection again.

Go back to the **hub** with the logo at the top left, tap the robot name (▾), and tap the robot's
row in **Select robot** to connect again. Once the dot is green and the status line reads
`Connected`, check whether the video returns.

## Right after a software update {#after-update}

**Cause:** After a robot software update without a reboot, the vision programs sometimes fail to
start properly.

**Fix:** **Reboot the robot** — `System reboot` under **Maintenance → Power / System**.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Rebooting cuts motor power and the robot sags to the ground. <strong>Sit it down first</strong>, make sure it is resting on the floor, and do not move it until the reboot finishes.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Still stuck {#still-stuck}

Tell us how far through steps 1–5 you got, and which sensors showed 0 fps in the **Vision sensors**
table.

**→ [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/payload_setting.html
================================================================================

# Payload configuration

Anything you mount on the robot shifts its center of mass, and the walk gets unsteady. Register the
**mass and center of mass** of the load in `Payload Configuration` under
**Robot settings › Payload setup**, and the walking dynamics account for it.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>Enter an <strong>approximate mass and center-of-mass height (Z)</strong> even when you do not know the exact figures. A rough value visibly steadies the walk, and <strong>leaving it empty is the worst case</strong>.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Before you start

- Put the robot on flat, stable ground.
- The app must be connected to the robot — without a connection it cannot read the slots.
- Know the load's mass and where its center of mass sits (X/Y/Z) relative to the robot body.

## What is on the screen

![Robot parameters — Payload Configuration](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/settings-robot.pc.en.png)

Wide screens show two columns; narrow ones stack them.

| Area | Contents |
|---|---|
| Top left | **3D preview** — registered payloads appear as markers. Tap a marker to select that slot; drag the X/Y/Z arrows to move it |
| Bottom left | **Editor for the selected slot** — `Mass`, `X`, `Y`, `Z`. With nothing selected it edits the first slot |
| Top right | **Slot table** — the slots the robot reports. `●` is a fixed payload, `◻` a user slot |
| Bottom right | **Total**, plus the `Get` and `Set Payload` buttons |

## Procedure

1. **Pick a slot.** Tap the slot you want in the table on the right. Ticking its checkbox marks it as
   **mounted** and fills in the catalogue defaults the robot holds for it.
2. **Enter the values.** In the editor on the left, set `Mass` (kg) and `X`, `Y`, `Z` (m). Tap a field
   to type a number, or use `−` and `+`. The **Interval** chips at the top right of the editor
   (`0.001`, `0.01`, `0.1`, `1`) set how much each press moves the value.
3. **Check the total.** The total box below the editor shows the combined mass and center of mass. If
   the total goes over the limit it turns red and `Set Payload` is disabled.
4. **Press `Set Payload`**, then confirm with **`Apply`**. The confirmation repeats the number of
   mounted slots and the totals. **Unticked slots are sent with mass 0, which clears them.**
5. Once applied the app re-reads the robot and shows *Applied (re-confirmed with robot values)*. The
   new values reach the walking dynamics immediately and are ramped in over one to two seconds.

`Get` re-reads the slots stored on the robot — **any edits in progress are discarded.**

## Allowed ranges

The bottom line of the editor always shows the range the connected robot allows. Robots whose
software does not report its limits fall back to the values below.

| Item | Range |
|---|---|
| Mass per slot | 0 – 20 kg |
| Total | 20 kg or less |
| Center of mass | \|X\| ≤ 0.5 m, \|Y\| ≤ 0.3 m, \|Z\| ≤ 0.4 m |

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>After changing mass or center of mass, <strong>run the center-of-mass (ZMP) calibration again</strong>. The calibration is stored against the load that was on the robot at the time, so an earlier calibration no longer fits once the load changes. It lives under <strong>Robot settings › Calibration</strong>.</p>
</div>
</div>

## When it does not work

| Message on screen | What it means and what to do |
|---|---|
| *Read failed — check robot connection* | There is no connection to the robot. Check [Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html) |
| *Legacy robot — 13 slots unsupported* | The robot software predates the slot API. Run a [robot software update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/software-update.html) and try again |
| *Total exceeds the 20 kg limit* | Remove a slot or lower a mass. Nothing is sent while the total is over |
| *Apply failed — out of range or disconnected* | A value is outside the ranges above, or the connection dropped mid-send |

Some robots already account for their fixed equipment in the robot-side configuration and therefore
expose **only one user slot**. A slot count that differs from what you expect is normal — use it as is.

## Still stuck {#still-stuck}

Tell us which slots you filled in with what, the total you had, and the message shown on screen.

**→ [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/robot-drifts.html
================================================================================

# Robot drifts to one side

You command the robot to walk straight and it veers to one side, or its body looks tilted
while standing. There is no single cause, so work through the steps **in order** — the
earlier ones are both more common and quicker to check.

## 1. Floor and initial pose {#floor-and-pose}

**Cause:** On a sloped or slippery floor the robot drifts sideways. Starting from an initial
pose that is not left-right symmetric has the same effect.

**Fix:** Try again on a flat, solid floor. Before switching the power on, check that the legs
are folded symmetrically.

**→ [Initial Pose](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/initial-pose.html)**

## 2. Payload configuration {#payload}

**Cause:** If equipment is mounted on the robot but its mass and position were never entered —
or entered incorrectly — the robot miscalculates its center of mass and drifts. Leftover
values after removing equipment cause the same problem.

**Fix:** Check that the configured values match what is actually mounted, and re-enter them if
they differ. If all equipment has been removed, reset the values.

**→ [Payload configuration](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/payload_setting.html)**

## 3. ZMP calibration {#zmp}

**Cause:** If the center of ground reaction force is off while the robot stands, it keeps
leaning to one side while walking too. This is the item that acts most directly on drift.

**Fix:** Run ZMP calibration again, on a flat solid floor with nothing mounted on the robot.

**→ [Calibration & Tuning](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/calibration-tuning.html)**

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Do not push the robot or place objects on it during calibration. Calibrating in that state makes the drift worse.</p>
</div>
</div>

## 4. Leg module condition {#leg-module}

**Cause:** A leg module or foot that has worked loose or worn down pushes the robot that way.

**Fix:** Sit the robot down, switch the power off, then check by hand whether any leg has play
and whether one foot pad is noticeably more worn than the others.

**→ [Leg Module](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/leg-module.html) · [Foot](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/maintenance/foot.html)**

## Still stuck? {#still-stuck}

Tell us how far through steps 1–4 you got, along with:

- which direction it drifts (left, right, forward, backward)
- whether it is already tilted while standing, or only drifts while walking
- whether it only happens in a particular gait mode

**→ [Contact us](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/sdk-build.html
================================================================================

# SDK Build Issues

## CMake install fails with `DDSC_RUNTIME_LOCATION-NOTFOUND`

```
CMake Error: file INSTALL cannot find ".../DDSC_RUNTIME_LOCATION-NOTFOUND"
```

**Cause:** ROS 2 is sourced in the current terminal (e.g. via `/etc/profile` or `~/.bashrc`). This causes `find_package(CycloneDDS)` to pick up ROS 2's system CycloneDDS from `/opt/ros/humble/`, which does not set `IMPORTED_LOCATION_RELEASE` in its CMake targets — so the install step fails.

**Fix:** Build in a terminal where ROS 2 is not sourced:

```bash
# Open a new terminal without sourcing ROS 2, then:
bash scripts/build.bash --no-cache
```

To temporarily disable ROS 2 in the current terminal:

```bash
unset ROS_VERSION ROS_DISTRO AMENT_PREFIX_PATH COLCON_PREFIX_PATH
export CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$(echo $CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v ros | tr '\n' ':' | sed 's/:$//')
export PATH=$(echo $PATH | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v ros | tr '\n' ':' | sed 's/:$//')
```

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/stair-mode-not-moving.html
================================================================================

# Stair mode not moving

You push the joystick in stair mode and the robot does not walk forward.
The most common cause is that camera data is not coming through.

## First checks {#first-checks}

- Confirm on screen that the mode actually changed to stair mode.
- Confirm you are using the **L stick**.
- Confirm **camera video is coming through normally**.

## Pushing the R stick forward does not move the robot {#r-stick}

**Cause:** In stair mode, forward and backward are handled by the **L stick**. This is by design, not a fault.

**Fix:** Use the controls below.

| Control | Action |
|---|---|
| L stick forward / back | Walk forward / backward |
| L stick left / right | Strafe |
| R stick left / right | Turn in place |

See [Basic Motion Commands](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html) for the controls of each mode.

## Without camera video the robot does not move {#no-camera}

**Cause:** Stair mode works from camera data. If there is no camera video, the robot does not
move however far you push the joystick.

**Fix:** Tap the status light next to the logo in the control home's top bar and check the
**Vision** row of **Overall system status**. If no video is coming through, work through
[No camera view](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/no-camera-view.html) first.

## Still stuck? {#still-stuck}

Open **[Logs → Real Time](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/logs.html#real-time)** and send us the messages logged at the moment
you pressed the stair mode button.

**→ [Contact us](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/steamdeck-setup.html
================================================================================

# Steam Deck reset & reinstall

The Steam Deck ships fully configured, so this procedure is not normally needed. Follow it
after a factory reset, or to install the RBQ app on a Steam Deck of your own. It also gets you
back to a known state when the controller will not boot properly or its configuration has
been messed up.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>A factory reset <strong>erases all user data and configuration and reinstalls SteamOS</strong>. Back up your settings and files first.</p>
</div>
</div>

## 1. Factory reset {#factory-reset}

If the device still boots normally, you can restore it to factory state from the OS settings.

1. Press the **Steam** button.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Go to the **System** tab.
4. Scroll to the bottom and select **Factory reset** under **Advanced**.
5. Press the **Factory Reset** button to confirm.

When the reset finishes, create a Steam account and sign in.

## 2. Switch to desktop mode {#desktop-mode}

1. Press the **Steam** button.
2. Select the **Power** menu.
3. Press **Switch to Desktop**.

## 3. Download the app {#download}

In desktop mode, open the [Downloads](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/downloads/) page in a browser and download
**RBQ Controller (Linux · Steam Deck)**. The file is `rbq-controller-x86_64.AppImage`.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p><strong>This first download can go in any folder.</strong> Run it once as described below, then press <strong>Install online</strong> inside the app: it creates its own install folder under <code>/home/deck/Documents/RBQ/</code> and points a <code>latest</code> link at it. Later updates only move that link, so <strong>the shortcut you add to Steam keeps working.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>

## 4. Make it executable {#permission}

Once downloaded, right-click `rbq-controller-x86_64.AppImage`, go to **Properties → Permissions**,
and tick **Is executable**.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/gui/steamdeck-2a.png' alt='Selecting Properties from the AppImage right-click menu' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Right-click → Properties</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/gui/steamdeck-2b.png' alt='Ticking the executable permission on the Permissions tab' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Permissions → Is executable</figcaption>
</figure>

## 5. Add it to Steam {#add-to-steam}

Right-click the same file again and choose **Add to Steam**.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/gui/steamdeck-3.png' alt='Selecting Add to Steam from the AppImage right-click menu' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Right-click → Add to Steam</figcaption>
</figure>

## 6. Boot into SteamOS and launch {#launch}

1. Use the **Steam icon** at the bottom left → **Shut Down**, then boot back into SteamOS.
2. Press the **STEAM** button at the bottom left and go to **Library → Non-Steam**.
3. Launch **rbq-controller** from the list.

Once the app is up, press **Install online** under **Robot settings → Software update** to create the
install folder — app updates then happen from that same screen.

For connecting to the robot from here, see
[Controller and Wi-Fi Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/operation/controller-wifi-connect.html).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/user-pc-connection.html
================================================================================

# Cannot connect to the user PC

NoMachine will not connect to the PC you work on directly. **The U-PC and the AI PC are the
same user PC**, and the address is determined by **where it sits**, not by what it is called.

| Location | IP |
|---|---|
| **Inside** the robot | `192.168.0.12` |
| **Outside** the robot | `192.168.0.13` |

The user PC is an option, so some robots do not have one.

## First checks {#first-checks}

- Check whether the user PC sits **inside or outside** the robot, and connect to the matching address above.
- Confirm the PC you are connecting from is on the **same network** as the robot — it must be connected to the robot's Wi-Fi (the name starts with `RBQ_`).
- Confirm the user PC is powered on.

## The address differs from the table {#check-ip}

**Cause:** If the user PC is using an address other than the one in the table, the connection fails.

**Fix:**

1. **Connect a monitor directly to the user PC** and check its current IP.
2. If it differs from the table, **set it statically** to the address matching its location.
3. Connect again with NoMachine.

See [Network Diagrams](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/interface/network.html) for the robot's full IP layout.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>The Motion PC (<code>192.168.0.10</code>) runs the robot itself and is <strong>not user-accessible.</strong> Do your development work on the user PC.</p>
</div>
</div>

## The network is reachable but no desktop appears {#session-fails}

**Cause:** NoMachine is not installed on the user PC, or its server is not running.

**Fix:** Follow the installation and connection procedure below.

**→ [How to Connect to the RBQ Development PC](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/release-note/how-to-connect-rbq-dev-pc.html)**

## Still stuck? {#still-stuck}

Tell us the IP you read from the monitor attached to the user PC, along with the error message
shown when the connection fails.

**→ [Contact us](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/version-rollback.html
================================================================================

# Version rollback

When a new version causes a problem and you need to go back. Rolling back uses **the same screen and
the same steps** as updating — pick a lower version from the list; nothing prevents it.

## Before you roll back {#before}

- Know the **version number** you want to go back to.
- **The app and the robot are separate targets.** Decide which one you are rolling back.
- Rolling back the robot requires a reboot, so work **somewhere you can sit the robot down**.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Robot software <strong>only takes effect after a reboot.</strong> Rebooting cuts motor power and the robot sags to the ground — <strong>sit it down first</strong>, make sure it is resting on the floor, and do not move it until the reboot finishes. While the robot is standing it ignores the reboot command and <strong>the app shows no error.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>

## Rolling back the robot {#rollback-robot}

![Robot settings → Software update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/app/settings-sw.pc.en.png)

1. Put the controller on a **Wi-Fi network with internet** (not the robot's).
2. Open **Robot settings → Software update**.
3. Press `Check versions` to fetch the list, then `Download` on the **earlier version** you want. The
   downloaded file stays on the device.
4. Reconnect the controller to the **robot Wi-Fi** (the network starting with `RBQ_`).
5. Check that the `Update file` card holds that version and that `Target` is `Motion`.
6. Press `Send robot software`, then `Send` in the confirmation dialog.
7. When the transfer finishes it offers a reboot. **Sit the robot down**, then press `Reboot now`.
8. Reconnect and check that `Version` on the `Current robot` card is the version you rolled back to.

Every item on that screen is described in [Software Update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/software-update.html).

## Rolling back the app {#rollback-app}

How you roll back depends on how the app was installed.

| Install route | How to roll back |
|---|---|
| **Desktop · Steam Deck** | `Download` the earlier version on the same screen, then switch to it with `Install app` on that row |
| **Android (APK installed directly)** | Get the earlier APK from [Downloads](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/downloads/) and install it |
| **Google Play · App Store** | **Stores do not offer earlier versions.** If you must roll back, use the direct install above |

The badge on the `GUI Version` line tells you which build you are on — no badge for a release,
`NIGHTLY` for a nightly, `LOCAL` for a local build with no release channel. **Only the last 10 days
of nightly builds are kept, so you cannot roll back to a nightly older than that** — pick a release
version instead.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>Downloading a version needs <strong>internet</strong>; sending it to the robot needs the <strong>robot Wi-Fi</strong>. Download first, then switch networks.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Rolling back without internet {#offline}

On a closed network, roll back from a file.

1. Somewhere with internet, download the `RBQ-<version>.tar.gz` for the version you want and put it
   on a USB drive.
2. On the software update screen press `Load from USB or file` and pick that file.
3. Continue from step 5 of [Rolling back the robot](#rollback-robot).

The file name must follow `RBQ-<version>.tar.gz` — the robot refuses anything else.

## After rolling back {#after}

- Check that the version on the `Current robot` card and the `GUI Version` are the ones you intended.
- Stand the robot up and confirm the [basic motions](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html) behave normally.
- If there is no camera image, see [No camera view](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/no-camera-view.html).

## Still stuck {#still-stuck}

Tell us the version before, the version you rolled back to, and the symptom that made you roll back.

**→ [Support](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/concept.html
================================================================================

# Concept

## System Diagram

<br/>
  <figure>
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/software/concept-diagram.png' alt='RBQ software concept diagram' />
  </figure>
<br/>

## SDK Overview

The **RBQ SDK** is built to provide developers with a flexible and scalable interface for working with the **RBQ quadruped robot**.

It supports both **low-level control** and **high-level commands**, so whether you're building your own controller or integrating the robot into an existing system, there's a suitable entry point.


## Low-Level Access
The **LV0 SDK** offers direct access to the robot’s sensors and actuators.

It is intended for developers who need **precise control** and **real-time feedback** from the hardware.

### Key Features:

- Read raw sensor data: IMU, joint encoders, etc.
- Send joint-level commands: position, velocity, torque
- Ideal for:
    - Custom controller development
    - Low-latency real-time experiments
    - Research in locomotion control


## High-Level Command Interface
The **LV1 SDK** provides a **simplified interface** to control the robot using predefined actions and commands, without needing to manage low-level details.

### Key Features:

- Execute common motions and gait behaviors with a single command
- Seamless integration with the **RBQ APP** command set
- APIs available in:
    - C/C++
    - Python
    - ROS2
- Ideal for:
    - Application developers
    - System integration
    - Rapid prototyping with minimal setup


## Supported Communication Interfaces
The SDK supports multiple communication protocols depending on your use case:

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Interface</th>
    <th>Description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>ROS2 SDK</td>
    <td>For robotics developers in the ROS2 ecosystem</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>DDS SDK</td>
    <td>For real-time, distributed communication using DDS</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>TCP / UDP</td>
    <td>Lightweight direct packet communication for custom tools</td>
  </tr>
</table>

# Developer's Guide

## Introduction

**Welcome to the RBQ simulation, command, and deploy/update manual**

This manual provides a comprehensive guide on how to **simulate** the RBQ robot, command it, and **deploy** your own algorithms to the real robot.

## Ready-to-use simulator and operator app for developers

- The RBQ robot can be simulated accurately using **MuJoCo**: "A fast and accurate physics engine suitable for advanced robotics simulation."

  📝 *Developers can modify the simulation environment "playground" by editing the file:* `resources/model/rbq_environment.xml`

- You command and monitor the robot with the **RBQ** app — the same app you use on real hardware, so anything you rehearse against the simulator carries over unchanged.
  - It shows robot status and sensor state, and takes touch, gamepad, or keyboard input.
  - Get it from the **[Downloads](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/downloads/)** page. The whole app is documented under [RBQ App](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/introduction.html).

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>This repository ships no on-PC control GUI. Earlier versions carried a <code>bin/GUI</code> maintenance tool; it is no longer published, and the <strong>RBQ</strong> app replaces it for every task in this guide.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Installation

  - This section explains how to install and set up the RBQ robot simulation and development environment from scratch.

### Requirements
To run the RBQ simulation and deployment environment smoothly, the following requirements are recommended:
* OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (x86)

   ![Ubuntu 22.04](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/software/ubuntu22-logo.png)

* Minimum PC specs:
  * CPU: Intel Core i7 - 12th Gen
  * RAM: 16 GB
  * Storage: 25 GB
* Control Devices
  * Keyboard: W, A, S, D, Q, E keys, and the arrow keys
  * Joystick: Logitech Wireless Gamepad F710 (Recommended)

   ![Logitech Wireless Gamepad F710](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/images/software/logitech-f710.jpeg)
  
### 1. Download the RBQ Repository

* Clone the repository and navigate to the open-source package:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RainbowRobotics/RBQ.git
cd RBQ
```

> All scripts, binaries, and SDK code are inside `RBQ/`. Run all commands from this directory.

> **Note:** Pre-built binaries ship in `bin-x86_64/` (and `bin-aarch64/` for arm64). No compilation step is required.

## ▶ Simulation

* The simulator runs in Docker — Docker is the only thing to install, and the script offers to install it when it is missing. The first run takes a few minutes to build its image. See [MuJoCo](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/simulator/mujoco.html).

* Start the **RBQ control modules and the MuJoCo simulator** together from `RBQ/`:

```bash
bash scripts/sim.bash --no-gui --vision
```

**NOTE:** *`ARGUMENTS:`*
* `--help`      : Display help message and exit.
* `--vision`    : Run vision modules (e.g., vision sensors, climb stairs enabled).
* `--no-gui`    : Skip the on-PC GUI. Pass this — the published repository does not carry one.

* It runs in the foreground of this terminal; Ctrl-C stops it. If Docker needs `sudo` on this PC, enter your password when asked.

### Initialize - Connect and Start the Simulated Robot

Start the **RBQ** desktop app **on the same PC** as the simulator. With no robot network around, the app finds the MuJoCo simulator on this PC by itself and connects — see [Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html).

1. Press **Control** on the hub to open the control home.
2. Tap the green **Auto Start** pill, press **Auto Start** in the dialog, and wait for the sequence to report **Done**. Press **Close**.
3. Press `STAND` on the motion card. The robot stands up and is ready for further commands.

  - 📝 *Depending on the posture it starts from, standing up can take a second.*

### Drive the Robot

The motion card carries `SIT`, `STAND`, `WALK`, and `STAIRS`, and the dashed **Motions** button opens the full grid, where `Wave` and `Run` live. What the joysticks do depends on which motion is running — standing, they adjust posture; walking, they drive.

**→ [Motion commands](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/motion-commands.html)** has a per-gait axis table, and **[Control home](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/control-home.html)** covers the rest of the screen, including keyboard driving on a PC.

## Real Robot

This section explains how to operate the **real RBQ robot**.

📖 *For detailed operation steps, refer to the [Operation Guide](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/guides/common/initial-pose.html)*

### 1. Connect to the Robot

* Connect your PC to the robot's Wi-Fi.
  
  📝 *Wi-Fi SSID: `RBQ_xxxx`.*


### 2. Start Robot Control in the App

Open the **RBQ** app and pick the robot in the robot list — see [Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/connection.html). The status line reads `Connected` with the route once it is talking to the robot.

* Press **Control** to open the control home.
* Tap **Auto Start**, press **Auto Start** in the dialog, and wait for **Done**. The robot is now activated and ready for operation.

### 3. Commands are exactly the same as in simulation
  - 📝 *It is strongly recommended to practice commanding the robot in the simulator first.*


## Update the Robot

Robot software is updated from the app. On the `Software update` screen, press
**`Send robot software`** — the robot deploys it as soon as the transfer completes, and the app
then offers a reboot.

**→ [Robot Software Update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/software-update.html)**

The app itself is updated from the `This app` section of the same screen.

**→ [App update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/software-update.html)**

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Put the robot in the <strong>sitting</strong> state before restarting, and do not move it until the restart finishes. Running a mismatched binary and script combination can cause unexpected behavior.</p>
</div>
</div>

`scripts/deploy.bash` is used for local development only — it copies freshly built
binaries into `~/rbq_ws/` on the machine you run it on:

```bash
bash scripts/deploy.bash --local
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--help` | Display help message and exit |
| `--local` | Deploy to `~/rbq_ws/` on the same PC |
| `--pro [FILES...]` | Deploy only the named binaries |

# Media

## Video

📥 Quick and easy access to the robot's video stream data.

Receive the available RTSP video streams using the following commands in your terminal.

### Current view

Mirrors whatever view the operator GUI currently has selected.

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 rtspsrc location='rtsp://192.168.0.10:8554/live' latency=100 ! application/x-rtp, media=video, encoding-name=H264 ! rtph264depay ! h264parse ! avdec_h264 ! xvimagesink
```

::: tip 📝 NOTE
The `front` and `rear` paths are off by default. Set `RTSP_FRONT` / `RTSP_REAR` to `true` in
`~/.config/RBQ/Streamer.ini` on the robot (created on the Streamer's first run; restart the Streamer after editing).
:::

### Front camera

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 rtspsrc location='rtsp://192.168.0.10:8554/front' latency=100 ! application/x-rtp, media=video, encoding-name=H264 ! rtph264depay ! h264parse ! avdec_h264 ! xvimagesink
```

### Rear camera

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 rtspsrc location='rtsp://192.168.0.10:8554/rear' latency=100 ! application/x-rtp, media=video, encoding-name=H264 ! rtph264depay ! h264parse ! avdec_h264 ! xvimagesink
```

### Thermal camera

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 rtspsrc location='rtsp://192.168.0.10:8554/thermal' latency=100 ! application/x-rtp, media=video, encoding-name=H264 ! rtph264depay ! h264parse ! avdec_h264 ! xvimagesink
```

::: tip 📝 NOTE
The **PTZ payload** must be loaded on the robot to access the thermal video stream, and
`RTSP_THERMAL` must be set to `true` in `~/.config/RBQ/Streamer.ini` on the robot
(created on the Streamer's first run; restart the Streamer after editing).
:::

## PTZ Camera

The streams above are published by the robot's own Streamer (`192.168.0.10:8554`). The PTZ payload's
camera also serves its own RTSP stream directly at `192.168.0.100:554`, alongside SUNAPI and ONVIF
control — see [PTZ Camera API](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/ptz-camera-api.html).

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/ptz-camera-api.html
================================================================================

# PTZ Camera API

The PTZ camera is a standalone [Hanwha Vision XNZ-L6320AG](https://www.hanwhavision.com/ko/products/product-details/XNZ-L6320AG) and is controlled **directly**, without going through the robot's software. It sits on the robot's internal network (default `192.168.0.100`) and supports three standard interfaces:

- **RTSP** — live H.264 / H.265 video
- **SUNAPI** — Hanwha's HTTP CGI API for pan / tilt / zoom, presets, focus, and audio
- **ONVIF** — Profile S / T for third-party VMS and tools

For the camera's mechanical and optical specifications, see [PTZ Camera](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/related-products/ptz-camera.html).

## Control paths {#control-paths}

There are two ways to drive the PTZ camera from code.

| | Directly to the camera (this page) | Through the robot (ROS2 / DDS) |
|---|---|---|
| Interfaces | SUNAPI (HTTPS CGI) · RTSP · ONVIF Profile S / T | `/rbq/cmd/ptz` · `/rbq/ptz` (`std_msgs/Float64MultiArray`) |
| Endpoint | The camera at `192.168.0.100` | The robot's DDS domain |
| Pan / tilt / zoom | Absolute and continuous moves, presets, focus | Absolute pan / tilt / zoom setpoint — **all three applied together** |
| Video | Camera RTSP, H.264 / H.265, profile-selectable | Robot Streamer RTSP — see [Media](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/media.html) |
| Audio | Speaker and microphone (SUNAPI audio, RTSP back-channel) | Not available |
| Third-party VMS | ONVIF | Not available |
| Requires | A camera account and access to the robot's internal network | The `Ptz` app running on the robot |

Use the [ROS2 topics](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/sdk/ros/topics.html#vision-ptz-camera) when the camera moves as part of
robot SDK code. Use direct control when you need the camera's own features — presets, focus, audio,
or ONVIF.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-caution-i" aria-hidden="true">!</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">Credentials</p>
<p>The camera uses HTTP <strong>Digest</strong> authentication (the SUNAPI default). The
<code>--anyauth</code> flag in the examples lets <code>curl</code> negotiate it automatically — a
plain <code>-u</code> sends Basic only and is rejected with <strong>401</strong>. Use the account
provided with your robot and replace <code>&lt;user&gt;</code> / <code>&lt;password&gt;</code>. Keep
the camera on a trusted network.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Live Video (RTSP) {#live-video-rtsp}

```bash
ffplay "rtsp://<user>:<password>@192.168.0.100:554/profile2/media.smp"
```

The profile number selects the stream (resolution / codec); the camera lists its profiles in its
own web UI.

## Pan / Tilt / Zoom (SUNAPI) {#pan-tilt-zoom-sunapi}

SUNAPI is served over HTTPS. The camera ships with a self-signed certificate, so `-k` (skip
verification) is used below. Common calls:

```bash
# Read the current zoom level
curl -k --anyauth -u <user>:<password> \
  "https://192.168.0.100/stw-cgi/ptzcontrol.cgi?msubmenu=query&action=view&Channel=0&Query=Zoom"

# Absolute zoom to 8x  (range 1-32)
curl -k --anyauth -u <user>:<password> \
  "https://192.168.0.100/stw-cgi/ptzcontrol.cgi?msubmenu=absolute&action=control&Zoom=8"

# Continuous zoom: in / stop / out  ->  1 / 0 / -1
curl -k --anyauth -u <user>:<password> \
  "https://192.168.0.100/stw-cgi/ptzcontrol.cgi?msubmenu=continuous&action=control&Zoom=1"
```

Pan, tilt, and presets use the same `ptzcontrol.cgi` endpoint with `Pan` / `Tilt` parameters and
`msubmenu=preset`. For the complete command set — pan/tilt ranges, presets, focus, audio in/out,
event, and image settings — see the **Hanwha SUNAPI** reference for the XNZ-L6320AG.

## Speaker & Microphone {#speaker-microphone}

The 25 W speaker and the microphone are the camera's own two-way audio, available over SUNAPI audio
and the RTSP back-channel. See the Hanwha SUNAPI reference for audio in/out.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>These interfaces talk to the camera directly. The robot's own software also reads the camera to
build its composite views, but that path is internal — integrations use the standard interfaces
above or the ROS2 PTZ topics.</p>
</div>
</div>

## See also {#see-also}

- [PTZ Camera](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/related-products/ptz-camera.html) — mechanical, optical, and thermal specifications
- [PTZ camera](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/ptz.html) — operating the camera from the app
- [Topic Reference — Vision — PTZ Camera](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/sdk/ros/topics.html#vision-ptz-camera) — robot-mediated pan / tilt / zoom over ROS2
- [Media](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/software/media.html) — RTSP streams published by the robot itself

# How to Connect to the RBQ Development PC

This guide explains how to connect to the **RBQ Dev PC** using **NoMachine** for remote desktop access.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>The <strong>RBQ Dev PC</strong> is the on-robot <strong>User-PC module</strong> — the machine you develop on. The User-PC module is an <strong>option</strong>, so your robot may not have one.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Step 1. Download NoMachine

1. Download the NoMachine application from the official website:
   🔗 [NoMachine Download Page](https://www.nomachine.com/)

2. Be sure to select the correct version for your platform (Linux).


## Step 2. Install NoMachine on the RBQ Dev PC

Open a terminal and run the following commands to install NoMachine:

```bash
cd /usr
sudo tar zxvf ~/Downloads/nomachine_latest_version.tar.gz
sudo /usr/NX/nxserver --install
sudo /usr/NX/bin/nxserver --status
```

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>Use <code>nxserver --status</code> to verify that the server is running properly.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Step 3. Connect from Your Development PC

1. Make sure your **development PC is connected to the same network** as the RBQ (via Ethernet or SSH-enabled connection).

2. Launch the **NoMachine app** on your PC.

3. Click <strong>"Add"</strong> to create a new connection.

4. Fill in the following details:

```
Name : rbq
Host : 192.168.0.12
```

The U-PC's address depends on where it is mounted: **`192.168.0.12` when mounted inside the robot**, **`192.168.0.13` when it sits outside**. If you cannot connect, attach a monitor to the U-PC and check its current IP. If it is using a different address, set it statically to the address above.

Please [contact us](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/support/) if it still does not connect.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>Recommended Nomachine Display Resolution Settings:</p><ul><li>✅ Enable: <strong>"Scale the remote desktop to fit the window"</strong></li><li>🚫 Disable: <strong>"Resize the remote display"</strong></li></ul>
</div>
</div>

## You're Now Connected!

You can now control and develop on the **RBQ Dev PC** remotely via a user-friendly desktop interface.

Enjoy your development workflow!

# Release Notes

User-facing changes in each released version, newest first. Every entry corresponds to a
change that shipped in that release.

<div class="sb sb-note">

## Stable and nightly {#channels}

RBQ software ships on two tracks. The release notes above cover **stable**.

| | **Stable** (tagged release) | **Nightly** |
|---|---|---|
| Version string | `vX.Y.Z` | `vX.Y.Z-nightly.<8-char commit>` |
| Published | On release | **Every night, automatically** |
| Contains | Only changes that passed release validation | Everything developed up to that day |
| Retention | **Every version is kept** | **Only the newest** — each build overwrites the last |
| Release notes | Yes (the list above) | None — the source commit is recorded in `nightly.txt` |
| How to select | Default | Release channel selector in the app |

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p><strong>Run stable on robots you operate in the field.</strong> Nightly is built exactly the way stable is, but it <strong>does not go through release validation</strong> — it can contain behavior that is still being worked on.</p>
</div>
</div>

Before choosing nightly, note that:

- **You cannot go back to an earlier nightly.** The channel keeps only the newest build. To go
  back, pick a stable version and install that instead — see
  [Version rollback](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/troubleshooting/version-rollback.html).
- **The documentation is split the same way.** If you run nightly software, read the nightly docs
  below as well; the stable docs may not describe that behavior yet.
- The release channel selector lives behind **[developer mode](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/manual/gui/developer-mode.html)** (access level 2 or higher).

## Which docs am I reading? {#doc-channels}

Like the software, this site is published in two channels.

| Channel | URL | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| **stable** | `rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/` | Matches the latest released software |
| **nightly** | `rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/` | Work in progress — may describe unreleased behavior |

Switch between them with the channel selector in the top navigation. If you operate a robot in
the field, stay on **stable**.
